definition_zh: 向后的；落后的；向后
definition_en: directed toward the back, or less developed than others
core_image: 一个人倒着走路，脚跟先落地
scene: 操场上教练喊了一声口令。 The team took a backward step.
sceneCN: 这里 backward 是「向后的」（第 1 个义项：朝后方方向的）；句意是队伍向后退了一步。

derivatives.zh: 由 backward 加 -ly 构成，义为「向后地」
由 backward 加 -ness 构成，义为「落后」

senses.title: Toward the back
senses.definition: moving or facing toward the back
senses.definitionCN: 朝后方移动或面向后方
senses.example: The team took a backward step.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍向后退了一步。
senses.why: Backward is back plus the direction suffix -ward, so it literally means in the direction of the back.
senses.whyCN: backward 是 back 加方向后缀 -ward，字面意思就是「朝背部的方向」。

senses.title: Less developed
senses.definition: not as advanced as others
senses.definitionCN: 不如别的先进
senses.example: The region remained backward for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区几十年间一直落后。
senses.why: Someone facing backward is looking where others have already been, which became a metaphor for lagging behind.
senses.whyCN: 面朝后方的人看的是别人已经走过的地方，这就成了「落后」的比喻。

senses.title: Shy or slow to act
senses.definition: slow to learn or unwilling to act
senses.definitionCN: 学得慢或不愿行动
senses.example: He was not backward in asking questions.
senses.exampleCN: 他问起问题来一点也不怯。
senses.why: Holding back from action looks like moving backward, so the word also describes a hesitant or slow person.
senses.whyCN: 从行动中退缩看起来像往后退，所以这个词也形容迟疑或迟缓的人。

intro.en: Backward is a direction word built from back.
intro.cn: backward 是由 back 构成的方向词。

items.en: bæc meant 'the back'.
items.cn: bæc 意为「背部」。

items.en: the suffix -weard meant 'turned toward'.
items.cn: 后缀 -weard 意为「朝向」。

items.en: bakward meant 'toward the back'.
items.cn: bakward 意为「朝向后方」。

items.en: It extended to being less advanced.
items.cn: 它扩展到表示「不够先进」。

items.en: Backward is chiefly an adjective in American English.
items.cn: 在美式英语中 backward 主要作形容词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the back base; the near-meaning group gives rear and lagging words.
note.cn: 形近组都含 back 词基；近义组是表示后方与落后的词。

entries.definition: toward the back, in reverse
a copy or a supporter
the area behind
toward the rear
at the back of something
less advanced economically

normalIntro.en: Backward points the body and the economy in the same direction.
normalIntro.cn: backward 让身体与经济指向同一个方向。

normal.en: Backward and backwards both exist; British English likes the s form as an adverb.
normal.cn: backward 与 backwards 都存在，英式英语副词常用带 s 的形式。

normal.en: A backward glance means looking back briefly.
normal.cn: a backward glance 意为回头一瞥。

normal.en: A backward country is one that lags behind.
normal.cn: a backward country 指落后的国家。

normal.en: The suffix -ward marks direction.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ward 标记方向。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: BACK-ward.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

abstract.en: See a walker moving with heels first.
abstract.cn: 想象一个倒着走、脚跟先落地的人。

abstract.en: See a clock whose hands turn the other way.
abstract.cn: 想象指针反向转动的钟。

abstract.en: See a runner losing ground on a track.
abstract.cn: 想象跑道上的选手正在失去位置。

examples.en: The team took a backward step.
examples.cn: 队伍向后退了一步。

examples.en: The region remained backward for decades.
examples.cn: 这个地区几十年间一直落后。

examples.en: He was not backward in asking questions.
examples.cn: 他问起问题来一点也不怯。

dict_mnemonic.text: back（后面）加 -ward（朝向）：朝着背后去，就是向后；落在别人后面，就是落后。

root: 由 back「背部」加方向后缀 -ward「朝向」构成，中古英语作 bakward；由「朝后方」引申为「落后」与「迟疑」。

sensesIntro.en: Facing the rear, lagging behind and holding back are three readings of one direction.
sensesIntro.cn: 朝后、落后与退缩，是同一个方向的三种读法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walker moving with heels first.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个倒着走、脚跟先落地的人。

branches.en: a backward step
branches.cn: 后退一步

branches.en: a backward glance
branches.cn: 回头一瞥

branches.en: a backward region
branches.cn: 落后地区

branches.en: backward technology
branches.cn: 落后的技术

branches.en: not backward in asking
branches.cn: 问起问题不怯

intro.en: The -ward suffix means 'turned toward', as in backward and forward.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ward 意为「朝向」，如 backward 与 forward。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the word is English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词是英语本族词。

definition_zh: 错误地；不正确地；不公正地；冤枉地
definition_en: in a way that is mistaken, incorrect, or unfair
core_image: 标签贴反了的东西，被放进了另一个箱子
scene: 仓库里一摞贴错标签的箱子被搬上了另一辆货车，收件人根本不在那一边。 The parcel was wrongly sent to the old address.
sceneCN: 这里 wrongly 是「错误地；不正确地」（第 1 个义项：以搞错的方式）；句意为包裹被错误地寄到了旧地址。贴反标签、放进错箱子的东西，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wrongly 去掉后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「错误的；不对的」
由 wrong 加 -ful 构成，义为「不当的；非法的」
由 wrong 加 -ness 构成，义为「错误；不当」

senses.title: In a mistaken way
senses.definition: in a way that is not correct or not based on the facts
senses.definitionCN: 以不正确或不以事实为依据的方式
senses.example: The parcel was wrongly sent to the old address.
senses.exampleCN: 包裹被错误地寄到了旧地址。
senses.why: The -ly ending turns the crooked adjective into a description of how an action is carried out.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ly 把「歪的」形容词变成对动作如何进行的描述。

senses.title: In an unfair way
senses.definition: in a way that is unfair to someone or blames them without cause
senses.definitionCN: 以对某人不公或无缘无故指责的方式
senses.example: He was wrongly blamed for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 延误的责任被错误地推到了他身上。
senses.why: A deed that bends away from right is also unfair, so the adverb covers unjust treatment as well as error.
senses.whyCN: 偏离正道的做法同时也是不公平的，于是这个副词既指错误也指不义的对待。

senses.title: With a wrong meaning
senses.definition: in a way that gives a false meaning to words or actions
senses.definitionCN: 以给词语或行为赋予错误含义的方式
senses.example: Her silence was wrongly read as agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 她的沉默被误读成了同意。
senses.why: When meaning itself goes crooked, the reader rather than the writer is the one who acts wrongly.
senses.whyCN: 当意思本身走歪时，错的是读者而不是写的人。

senses.title: Against the rules
senses.definition: in a way that breaks a rule or a proper procedure
senses.definitionCN: 以违反规则或正当程序的方式
senses.example: The form was wrongly completed, so it had to be redone.
senses.exampleCN: 这张表填得不合规定，只好重填。
senses.why: Rules draw straight lines, so anything done off the line is done wrongly in a procedural sense.
senses.whyCN: 规则画出直线，凡偏离这条线去做的，在程序意义上就是 wrongly。

intro.en: Wrongly is the adverb formed from the adjective wrong with the native ending -ly, which English has used this way since the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: wrongly 是形容词 wrong 加本土后缀 -ly 构成的副词，英语自中世纪起就这样构词。

items.en: The base rangr meant twisted or contrary.
items.cn: 词基 rangr 意为扭曲的、反向的。

items.en: Wrong was used both as adjective and adverb, and -ly forms appeared beside it.
items.cn: wrong 兼作形容词与副词，旁边还出现带 -ly 的形式。

items.en: Wrongly specialised as the careful written adverb of error.
items.cn: wrongly 专门充当表示「错误」的书面副词。

items.en: Legal writing made wrongly accused and wrongly convicted fixed phrases.
items.cn: 法律文字让 wrongly accused 与 wrongly convicted 成了固定说法。

items.en: Everyday speech still prefers plain wrong, so wrongly sounds slightly formal.
items.cn: 日常口语仍偏爱不加 -ly 的 wrong，因此 wrongly 听起来略正式。

note.en: The first group holds forms of the same family, the second holds adverbs of error and unfairness.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词族的形式，第二组收表示错误与不公的副词。

entries.definition: Not correct or not right.
Unfair or against the law.
The quality of being wrong.
Because of a mistake in thinking.
In a way that is not correct.
In a way that is not just.

normalIntro.en: Wrongly is wrong plus -ly: the silent w stays, and the ending tells you it describes an action.
normalIntro.cn: wrongly 是 wrong 加 -ly：不发音的 w 仍保留，词尾说明它修饰动作。

normal.en: Wrongly is the written adverb; plain wrong is the spoken one.
normal.cn: wrongly 是书面副词，口语里直接用 wrong。

normal.en: The phrase wrongly accused appears in news reports about courts.
normal.cn: wrongly accused 常出现在关于法庭的新闻报道里。

normal.en: The -ly ending never changes the silent w.
normal.cn: -ly 词尾不会改变不发音的 w。

normal.en: Wrongly blamed means the blame landed in the wrong place.
normal.cn: wrongly blamed 指责任落到了错的人身上。

normal.en: Use wrongly with past participles such as spelt and labelled.
normal.cn: wrongly 常与 spelt、labelled 等过去分词连用。

abstract.en: A label stuck on the wrong box.
abstract.cn: 贴在错误箱子上的标签。

abstract.en: A name crossed out on a form and replaced by another.
abstract.cn: 表格上一个被划掉、换成另一个的名字。

abstract.en: A quiet person hearing a verdict that describes someone else.
abstract.cn: 一个沉默的人听到了一段说的是别人的判词。

examples.en: The letter was wrongly addressed and came back a week later.
examples.cn: 这封信地址写错了，一周后被退回。

examples.en: He was wrongly accused of taking the money.
examples.cn: 他被冤枉拿了那笔钱。

examples.en: Several words in the sign were wrongly spelt.
examples.cn: 牌子上的几个词拼错了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「荣利」——追荣利追得太急，路就走歪了。

root: 由形容词 wrong（古诺斯语 rangr，扭的、歪的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，字面义为「以歪的方式」，即错误地、不公正地。

sensesIntro.en: A mistaken action comes first, then unfair treatment, then misread meaning, then broken procedure.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是做错的动作，再是不公的对待，然后是读错的意思，最后是违反的程序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a label stuck on the wrong box.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴在错误箱子上的标签。

branches.en: The error branch: action taken on false facts.
branches.cn: 错误分支：依据错误事实采取的行动。

branches.en: The justice branch: blame placed on the innocent.
branches.cn: 公正分支：责任落到无辜者身上。

branches.en: The meaning branch: words taken in a false sense.
branches.cn: 意义分支：词语被理解成错的意思。

branches.en: The procedure branch: a step taken off the straight line.
branches.cn: 程序分支：偏离直线的一步。

branches.en: The shared branch: both error and injustice start as a bent line.
branches.cn: 共同分支：错误与不公都始于一条弯线。

intro.en: Wrongly is a transparent adjective plus -ly; the base is a Norse stem that stays unchanged before the suffix.
intro.cn: wrongly 是形容词直接加 -ly 的透明结构；词基是诺斯语词干，加后缀前形状不变。

latinIntro.en: The base is not Latin, so the words below are related concepts rather than ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 词基并非拉丁语，因此下面这些词是相关概念而非祖先。

items.example: The base supplies the whole meaning.
It changes the adjective into an adverb.
It forms wrongly blamed and wrongly accused.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wrongly blamed 与 wrongly accused。

items.example: Mistakenly carries the same idea from another prefix.
items.exampleCN: mistakenly 用另一个前缀表达同样的意思。

items.example: Unfairly is the close partner in the fairness sense.
items.exampleCN: unfairly 在「公平」义上是它的近邻。

items.example: It forms wrongness from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由同一词干构成 wrongness。

items.example: It is the legal flavoured partner of wrongly.
items.exampleCN: 它是 wrongly 带法律色彩的同族副词。

items.example: The adverb often describes how such acts happen.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词常说明这类行为是怎样发生的。

definition_zh: 令人向往的；可取的；有吸引力的
definition_en: worth having or doing because it is good or pleasant
core_image: 橱窗里挂着一件外套，灯光正好落在它的肩上
scene: 看房网站上那套房子照片明亮，采光、楼层和通勤时间都写得很清楚。 A quiet street and good light make the flat highly desirable.
sceneCN: 这里 desirable 指「令人向往的」（第 1 个义项：有吸引力、值得拥有）；句意是安静的街道与充足的光线让这套房子非常抢手。

pos.zh: 令人向往的；可取的；有吸引力的

senses.title: Worth wanting
senses.definition: attractive and pleasant enough to be wanted by many people
senses.definitionCN: 有吸引力、令人愉快，因而许多人都想要
senses.example: A quiet street and good light make the flat highly desirable.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的街道与充足的光线让这套房子非常抢手。
senses.why: A thing becomes desirable when imagining it feels better than not having it.
senses.whyCN: 当想着它比没有它更舒服，一件东西就变得令人向往。

senses.title: Worth doing
senses.definition: wise and useful enough to be worth choosing or doing
senses.definitionCN: 明智有用，因而值得选择或去做
senses.example: It is desirable to check the figures twice.
senses.exampleCN: 把数字核对两遍是可取的做法。
senses.why: The same pull works on actions: some choices feel lighter beforehand.
senses.whyCN: 同一种吸引力也作用于行动：有些选择事先就让人觉得更轻松。

intro.en: Desirable comes from Latin desiderabilis, from desiderare, to long for, a word the Romans linked to waiting for a favourable star.
intro.cn: desirable 来自拉丁语 desiderabilis，源于 desiderare（渴望），古罗马人把这个词与等待吉星联系起来。

items.en: Desiderare meant to long for something that was missing.
items.cn: desiderare 指渴望某件尚缺的东西。

items.en: Writers guessed it came from de- and sidus, a star, as in waiting for a good sign.
items.cn: 作家猜测它由 de- 与 sidus（星辰）构成，就像等待一个好兆头。

items.en: Desiderabilis described anything worth longing for.
items.cn: desiderabilis 形容任何值得渴望之物。

items.en: English took the word for things pleasing and worth having.
items.cn: 英语借来这个词，指令人愉快、值得拥有的东西。

items.en: It also grew a cooler sense: advisable rather than attractive.
items.cn: 它又长出一层较冷静的意思：不是说有吸引力，而是说可取。

note.en: The look-alike group all come from desire, and the meaning group ranges from plain attraction to what is wise to choose.
note.cn: 形近组都出自 desire 一族，近义组则从单纯的吸引力一路到明智的选择。

entries.definition: a strong wish for something
in a pleasing or suitable way
entries.definitionCN: 以令人满意或合适的方式

entries.definition: not wanted or not wise
entries.definitionCN: 不受欢迎的或不可取的

entries.definition: pleasant to look at or think about
entries.definitionCN: 看着或想着令人愉快的

entries.definition: sensible and likely to help
better and more worth choosing

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a lit shop window and end with a checklist that says this choice is wise.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从亮着灯的橱窗开始，落到一张写着这个选择很明智的清单。

normal.en: Desirable things glow a little before you own them.
normal.cn: 令人向往的东西，在你拥有之前会微微发亮。

normal.en: The word carries desire inside it like a coat carries a lining.
normal.cn: 这个词里头装着 desire，就像外套里缝着内衬。

normal.en: What many people want becomes desirable without being better.
normal.cn: 许多人都想要的东西会变得抢手，未必变得更好。

normal.en: A desirable choice is one that looks lighter the longer you hold it.
normal.cn: 可取的选择，是握得越久越觉得轻的那个。

normal.en: Add un- and the window light goes out.
normal.cn: 加上 un-，橱窗里的灯就灭了。

abstract.en: Picture a coat in a window with one shoulder lit.
abstract.cn: 想象橱窗里一件外套，只有一只肩膀被照亮。

abstract.en: Picture two roads, one of them slightly wider and smoother.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路，其中一条稍微宽一点、平一点。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching for a star it cannot touch yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向一颗还够不到的星。

examples.en: A quiet street and good light make the flat highly desirable.
examples.cn: 安静的街道与充足的光线让这套房子非常抢手。

examples.en: It is desirable to check the figures twice.
examples.cn: 把数字核对两遍是可取的做法。

examples.en: Patience is a desirable quality in a teacher.
examples.cn: 耐心是教师身上一种令人称道的品质。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 desirable 记成「地摘若宝」：desire 是渴望，able 是能，能让人渴望的，就是令人向往的。

root: 来自拉丁语 desiderabilis，源于 desiderare（渴望），由 de- 与 sidus（星辰）构成，古人把渴望与等待吉星相连。本义是值得盼望的，后来指有吸引力、令人愉快，也指做事明智可取。

sensesIntro.en: From a thing that pulls the eye, to a choice that quietly recommends itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一件牵住目光的东西，到一个悄悄自我推荐的选项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit object that the eye keeps returning to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件发着光、让人一再回望的东西。

branches.en: The first sense is the pull itself, pleasant and hard to ignore.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是那股吸引力，令人愉快，难以忽视。

branches.en: The second sense cools that pull into good advice.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把那股吸引力冷却成一句好建议。

branches.en: A home, a quality and a chance can all wear the same glow.
branches.cn: 一套房子、一种品质、一个机会，都能带上同样的光。

branches.en: Attraction and good sense both answer one question: is it worth having?
branches.cn: 吸引力与明智都在回答同一个问题：它值不值得要。

branches.en: When the answer is no, the same word simply takes un-.
branches.cn: 答案是否定时，这个词加上 un- 就够了。

intro.en: Desirable sits in a family of wanting, with forms for the wish itself and for what should be avoided.
intro.cn: desirable 处在一族表示「想要」的词里，既有愿望本身，也有应当避开的东西。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin desiderare, to long for, and -able adds the sense of being worth that longing.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 desiderare（渴望），后缀 -able 添上「值得被渴望」的意思。

items.example: She had a strong desire to travel.
They discussed the desirability of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他们讨论了这个计划的可取之处。
这些房间明亮得令人满意。

items.example: They noted the undesirability of the site.
items.exampleCN: 他们指出了这个选址的不妥。
这个房间暗得让人不满意。

definition_zh: 删除；删去；清除
definition_en: to remove written or stored material completely
core_image: 一行字在屏幕上闪了一下，然后整行消失
scene: 她按住退格键不放，整整一段文字飞快地缩短，最后只剩光标。 She deleted the whole paragraph with one key.
sceneCN: 这里 delete 指「删除」（第 1 个义项：把文字或文件彻底去掉）；句意是她一键删掉了整段文字。

senses.title: Remove a file or a line
senses.definition: to remove a file, message or line of text from a device
senses.definitionCN: 把文件、信息或文字行从设备上去掉
senses.example: She deleted the whole paragraph with one key.
senses.exampleCN: 她一键删掉了整段文字。
senses.why: What is gone from the screen is gone from the argument too.
senses.whyCN: 从屏幕上消失的东西，也从论证里消失了。

senses.title: Strike a word out of a text
senses.definition: to take out a word or passage from a piece of writing
senses.definitionCN: 从一篇文字里去掉某个词或一段话
senses.example: The editor deleted two long sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑删去了两个长句。
senses.why: Writing is choosing what the reader will never see.
senses.whyCN: 写作就是决定哪些东西读者永远看不到。

senses.title: Wipe out a record
senses.definition: to destroy stored information so it cannot be found
senses.definitionCN: 销毁存储的信息，使人再也找不到
senses.example: He deleted the old records from the system.
senses.exampleCN: 他把旧记录从系统里清除了。
senses.why: A memory kept in a machine can be taken away at once.
senses.whyCN: 存在机器里的记忆，可以一下子被拿走。

intro.en: Delete comes from Latin delere, to blot out, whose printer's mark dele told a reader to take a letter away.
intro.cn: delete 来自拉丁语 delere（抹去），印刷用的符号 dele 就是叫读者把字去掉。

items.en: Delere meant to wipe a surface clean of marks.
items.cn: delere 意为把表面上的痕迹擦干净。

items.en: The command dele was written on proofs to mean remove.
items.cn: 校样上写 dele，就是要求删掉。

items.en: English printers borrowed dele as a mark of deletion.
items.cn: 英国印刷工借来 dele，作为删除的记号。

items.en: The verb delete spread to any removal of writing.
items.cn: 动词 delete 扩展到一切去掉文字的行为。

items.en: Computers gave it a key of its own and a new home.
items.cn: 计算机给了它一个专属按键和新的家。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dele- opening, and the meaning group moves from taking out to rubbing away.
note.cn: 形近组共用 dele- 开头，近义组则从取出走到擦去。

entries.definition: a person sent to speak for a group
entries.definitionCN: 被派去代表团体发言的人

entries.definition: easily broken or needing care
entries.definitionCN: 容易破碎或需要小心对待的

entries.definition: to use up most of a supply
to take something away from its place
to rub out marks completely
to take a part away from the whole

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line vanishing from a screen and end with a record that no longer exists.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从屏幕上消失的一行字开始，落到一份已经不存在的记录。

normal.en: A deleted sentence leaves no echo, only a shorter page.
normal.cn: 删掉的句子没有回声，只留下一张更短的纸。

normal.en: The editor's pencil is a small knife with good manners.
normal.cn: 编辑的铅笔，是一把有礼貌的小刀。

normal.en: Backspace is quicker than regret and much cheaper.
normal.cn: 退格键比后悔快得多，也便宜得多。

normal.en: A file deleted is a room with the door painted over.
normal.cn: 被删的文件，是一间把门刷平了的屋子。

normal.en: Dele was a mark on paper before it was a key on a board.
normal.cn: dele 先是纸上的记号，后来才成了键盘上的键。

abstract.en: Picture a line of letters breaking into small square pieces.
abstract.cn: 想象一行字母碎成一个个小方块。

abstract.en: Picture a finger pressing one key and stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指按下一个键，然后停住。

abstract.en: Picture a name gone from a list, and the space still clean.
abstract.cn: 想象名单上少了一个名字，留下的地方很干净。

examples.en: She deleted the whole paragraph with one key.
examples.cn: 她一键删掉了整段文字。

examples.en: The editor deleted two long sentences.
examples.cn: 编辑删去了两个长句。

examples.en: He deleted the old records from the system.
examples.cn: 他把旧记录从系统里清除了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 delete 记成「得离题」：写离题的话，就该被删掉。

root: 源自拉丁语 delere（抹去、销毁），印刷时代用 dele 这个符号要求删字，后来才成为动词。它的核心一直是「把痕迹从表面上弄掉」，进入计算机时代后，删除文件与记录都沿用了这个老词。

sensesIntro.en: From a paragraph gone, to a word cut out, to a record wiped clean.
sensesIntro.cn: 从消失的一段文字，到被剪掉的一个词，再到被清空的记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of text that stops existing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一行字突然不再存在。

branches.en: The first sense is a file or line removed from a device.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把文件或文字行从设备上去掉。

branches.en: The second sense cuts a passage out of a text.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是从文章中剪去一段。

branches.en: The third sense clears stored memory away.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是把存储的记忆清空。

branches.en: Screen and page both lose something at a keystroke.
branches.cn: 屏幕与纸页都在一按之间少了点什么。

branches.en: Both senses leave a clean place where something stood.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在原处留下干净的一块。

intro.en: Delete gives English nouns of removal and a modern verb for bringing back what was removed.
intro.cn: delete 给英语送来表示删除的名词，以及一个把删掉内容恢复的现代动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is delere, to blot out, with de- meaning completely.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 delere（抹掉），前缀 de- 表示彻底。

items.example: The deletion left a small gap.
items.exampleCN: 删掉的地方留下一个小空档。

items.example: The deleted file was not missed.
items.exampleCN: 被删掉的文件没人想起。

items.example: The comment is deletable by the owner.
items.exampleCN: 这条评论可由本人删除。

items.meaning: to bring back a removed file
items.example: He undeleted the letter by mistake.
items.exampleCN: 他误操作把那封信恢复了。

items.meaning: a sign showing text should go
items.example: The deletion mark sat in the margin.
Accidental deletion lost the whole folder.
items.exampleCN: 误删把整个文件夹弄丢了。

items.example: She pressed the delete key twice.

definition_zh: 借此；由此；从而
definition_en: by that means, by that act, or as a result of that
core_image: 一根绳子从“那件事”牵到“这个结果”：动作在前，结果在后。
scene: 老城区挂出了禁行标志，空气监测屏上的曲线缓缓下降。 The city banned cars from the old quarter, thereby reducing air pollution.
sceneCN: 这里 thereby 是「从而、由此」（第 2 个义项：表示结果）；句意：该市禁止汽车进入老城区，从而使空气污染减少了三分之一。场景要点：禁行标志、无车的石板街、监测屏上的空气质量数字。

pos.zh: 借此；由此；从而（正式书面语）

collocations.zh: 这背后还有一段故事（古语）

senses.title: By that means
senses.titleCN: 借此：用那件事作为手段
senses.definition: by means of that action, tool, or arrangement; used to name the instrument that produces a result
senses.definitionCN: 通过那一动作、工具或安排；用于指出产生结果的手段
senses.example: They lowered the price and thereby attracted new customers.
senses.exampleCN: 他们降低了价格，借此吸引了新客户。
senses.why: There is the old locative 'that', and by is the preposition of means. Put together, thereby points to the thing just mentioned as the instrument.
senses.whyCN: there 是古英语的方位指示“那”，by 是表示手段的介词。两者合起来，thereby 就把刚提到的那件事指为工具。

senses.title: As a result of that
senses.titleCN: 由此：结果顺着动作落下
senses.definition: as a consequence of that action or fact, often introducing a participle clause
senses.definitionCN: 作为那一动作或事实的后果，常引导分词从句
senses.example: The rule was simplified, thereby reducing errors.
senses.exampleCN: 规则被简化，从而减少了错误。
senses.why: The same rope now runs from cause to effect rather than from agent to tool. English uses thereby with -ing clauses to mark the result that follows.
senses.whyCN: 同一根绳子现在从原因牵到结果，而不是从行动者牵到工具。英语用 thereby 加分词从句来标记随后出现的结果。

senses.title: Consequently, by that reasoning
senses.titleCN: 因此：按那条推理走下去
senses.definition: therefore, or as a logical consequence of what has just been said
senses.definitionCN: 因此，或作为刚说内容在逻辑上的后果
senses.example: The two events coincided, and thereby seemed connected.
senses.exampleCN: 两件事同时发生，因此看起来似乎有关联。
senses.why: A means can also be a premise: if you accept that, you are led to this. Thereby then works as a formal connector of reasoning rather than of physical action.
senses.whyCN: 手段也可以是前提：接受那一点，就会被引到这里。这时的 thereby 是推理的形式连接词，而不是物理动作的连接。

senses.title: By doing that
senses.titleCN: 借那一动作：方式即手段
senses.definition: by performing that particular act, especially when the act and its effect are one gesture
senses.definitionCN: 通过做出那一特定行为，尤指行为与效果是同一个动作
senses.example: She resigned, thereby avoiding a formal dismissal.
senses.exampleCN: 她辞职了，借此避免了被正式解雇。
senses.why: Here the means is not a tool but an act. Resigning and avoiding dismissal are the same movement seen from two sides, and thereby joins them.
senses.whyCN: 这里的手段不是工具，而是一个行为。辞职与避免解雇是同一动作的两面，thereby 把两面接在一起。

senses.title: By that fact alone
senses.titleCN: 凭那个事实：资格由此而来
senses.definition: by virtue of that fact or status, especially in legal or formal statements of entitlement
senses.definitionCN: 凭借那一事实或身份，尤用于法律或正式的权利陈述
senses.example: A person born there is a citizen, and thereby entitled to a passport.
senses.exampleCN: 在那里出生的人即为公民，并由此有权获得护照。
senses.why: The instrument is now a fact rather than an action. A status carries its consequences automatically, and thereby marks that automatic carry.
senses.whyCN: 工具现在是一个事实，而不是一个动作。身份会自动带来后果，thereby 标记的正是这种自动携带。

senses.title: In that respect
senses.titleCN: 在这一点上：就那方面而言
senses.definition: in that respect or by that provision, used in legal and older formal prose
senses.definitionCN: 在那一点上，或依据那项条款，用于法律与较早的正式文体
senses.example: The clause is void, and thereby the whole contract fails.
senses.exampleCN: 该条款无效，就此而言整份合同失效。
senses.why: This is the limiting use: thereby does not name a cause but marks the respect in which a statement holds. It survives mainly in legal writing.
senses.whyCN: 这是限定用法：thereby 不指出原因，而标记一句话在哪个方面成立。它主要残留在法律写作中。

senses.title: By which (archaic relative use)
senses.definition: by which, used in older English to introduce a relative clause about a means
senses.definitionCN: 凭借之，用于较早英语中引导关于手段的关系从句
senses.example: They built a channel thereby the water might reach the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 他们修了一条渠道，借此水可以到达田里。
senses.why: Before whereby became the standard relative form, thereby could do that work. The modern language has pushed this use to the edge of the grammar.
senses.whyCN: 在 whereby 成为标准关系形式之前，thereby 也能承担这个功能。现代英语已把这种用法推到语法的边缘。

senses.title: The academic result connector
senses.titleCN: 学术连接：分词前的结果标记
senses.definition: a formulaic connector in academic writing, typically followed by a participle to sum up a consequence
senses.definitionCN: 学术写作中的套式连接词，通常后接分词，概括某后果
senses.example: The samples were dried overnight, thereby preventing contamination.
senses.exampleCN: 样品被晾干过夜，从而防止了污染。
senses.why: Modern academic style fixed the pattern thereby + -ing. The old rope between act and result has become a punctuation mark of argument.
senses.whyCN: 现代学术文体固定了 thereby + -ing 的句式。那根连接动作与结果的旧绳子，变成了论证里的标点符号。

intro.en: Thereby is not a Latin word at all. It is an English compound of there, the old locative of 'that', and by, the preposition of means. The two were joined in Old and Middle English and later restricted to formal prose.
intro.cn: thereby 根本不是拉丁词，而是英语复合词：there 是“那”的古方位形式，by 是表示手段的介词。两者在古英语与中古英语中结合，后来被限制在正式书面语中。

items.en: Þǣr was the locative form of 'that', meaning 'there, in that place'. It is the ancestor of modern there and of the there- compounds.
items.cn: þǣr 是“那”的方位形式，意为“在那里”。它是现代 there 以及 there- 系列复合词的祖先。

items.en: Bī meant 'by, near, by means of'. It is the source of modern by and of the instrumental sense in thereby.
items.cn: bī 意为“在旁、靠近、凭借”。它是现代 by 的来源，也是 thereby 中手段义的来源。

items.en: A compound of the two is attested in Old English, though its frequency and exact range are uncertain. It already had the sense 'by that means'.
items.cn: 两者的复合形式在古英语中已有见，但其使用频率与确切范围存疑。它当时已含“借此、由此”之义。

items.en: Middle English therby carried the instrumental and result senses into general use. The spelling varied between ther-, thar-, and there-.
items.cn: 中古英语 therby 把手段义与结果义带入通用语。拼写在 ther-、thar-、there- 之间摇摆。

items.en: The modern spelling thereby settled in the 16th century. As whereby and wherein took over the relative function, thereby narrowed to means and result.
items.cn: 现代拼写 thereby 在十六世纪固定。随着 whereby、wherein 接管关系功能，thereby 缩小到手段与结果两义。

items.en: Today thereby is almost exclusively formal and written. Its most frequent pattern is thereby + -ing, summarizing the consequence of the main clause.
items.cn: 今天 thereby 几乎只用于正式书面语。最常见句式是 thereby + -ing，概括主句的后果。

note.en: The first group is the there- compound family, which is easy to confuse; the second separates connectors that also join cause and result.
note.cn: 第一组是易混淆的 there- 复合词家族；第二组区分同样连接因果的连接词。

entries.definition: by which; it introduces a clause naming the means. It has taken over the relative job that thereby once did.
entries.definitionCN: 凭借之；引导说明手段的从句。它接管了 thereby 曾经承担的关系功能。

entries.definition: in that document, place, or matter. It points inside something already mentioned.
entries.definitionCN: 在其中；在该文件、地点或事情中。它指向前文已提到之物的内部。

entries.definition: for that reason; consequently. It marks inference, while thereby marks means or result.
entries.definitionCN: 因此；所以。它标记推理，而 thereby 标记手段或结果。

entries.definition: immediately after that; as a result of that. It marks sequence in time more than means.
entries.definitionCN: 随即；因此。它更多标记时间上的先后，而非手段。

entries.definition: in this way or as a result. It is the closest formal partner and can replace thereby in many result clauses.
entries.definitionCN: 以这种方式；因此。它是最接近的正式伙伴，在许多结果从句中可替换 thereby。

entries.definition: as a result; therefore. It is a full sentence connector and does not attach to a participle as thereby does.
entries.definitionCN: 结果是；因此。它是完整的句子连接词，不像 thereby 那样接分词。

entries.definition: in a way that fits what has just been said. It adds the idea of adjusting a response.
entries.definitionCN: 相应地；因此。它增加了“调整应对”的意思。

entries.definition: for this reason; from this fact. It is more logical and less instrumental than thereby.
entries.definitionCN: 因此；由此。它比 thereby 更偏逻辑，更少手段意味。

entries.definition: for that reason or in that way. It is the everyday connector that thereby replaces in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 所以；这样一来。它是 thereby 在正式写作中替代的日常连接词。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: there 'that' + by 'by means of'. It is an English compound, not a Latin borrowing; the Latin entry list is empty by design.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：there“那”+ by“凭借”。它是英语复合词，不是拉丁借词，因此拉丁词条按实际情况留空。

normal.en: There + by: by that thing you just mentioned.
normal.cn: there + by：凭借你刚提到的那件事。

normal.en: Thereby reducing is the standard academic pattern: action first, result in the participle.
normal.cn: thereby reducing 是标准学术句式：先有动作，结果放在分词里。

normal.en: Whereby does the relative job; thereby does the means-and-result job.
normal.cn: whereby 干关系从句的活；thereby 干手段与结果的活。

normal.en: Thereby is not therefore: one names the instrument, the other names the inference.
normal.cn: thereby 不是 therefore：一个指出工具，一个指出推理。

normal.en: Thereby hangs a tale keeps the oldest flavour: by that fact there is a story.
normal.cn: thereby hangs a tale 保留了最古老的味道：由那件事，引出一段故事。

abstract.en: Thereby is grammar's way of tying an act to its shadow, the result.
abstract.cn: thereby 是语法把动作与它的影子——结果——绑在一起的方式。

abstract.en: A formal word for a simple thing: this, so that.
abstract.cn: 一个正式的词，说的却是极简单的事：这样，所以。

abstract.en: Every thereby hides a claim that the result really did follow.
abstract.cn: 每个 thereby 背后都藏着一个主张：结果确实随之而来。

examples.en: The firm automated its invoices, thereby cutting paperwork by half.
examples.cn: 公司实现了发票自动化，从而把文书工作减少了一半。

examples.en: He missed the deadline, thereby losing the deposit.
examples.cn: 他错过了截止日期，因此损失了定金。

examples.en: The two islands share a language and are thereby often treated as one region.
examples.cn: 这两座岛共享一种语言，因此常被当作一个地区。

dict_mnemonic.text: “得来拜”——得来全靠拜那一下，由此得结果 → thereby 借此、从而

root: 英语本土复合词：there“那”（古英语 þǣr 的方位形式）+ by“凭借、在旁”，合起来表示“借那件事、由此”。无拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of thereby, all one rope: the thing just named is tied to its means, its act, its consequence, its inference, or the respect in which it holds.
sensesIntro.cn: thereby 的八个义项都围绕同一根绳子：把刚提到的事，系到它的手段、行为、后果、推理，或它成立的那个方面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope running from a named act to the result it drags behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绳子从已被点名的事，牵到它拖在身后的结果。

branches.en: MEANS AND ACT: the instrument can be a tool or a deed, but in both cases it is what you use.
branches.cn: 手段与行为：工具可以是一件物，也可以是一个举动，但都是你所“用”的东西。

branches.en: RESULT: the rope runs forward into a consequence, most visibly in the academic thereby + -ing pattern.
branches.cn: 结果：绳子向前延伸到后果，最明显的就是学术体的 thereby + -ing 句式。

branches.en: INFERENCE AND ENTITLEMENT: from a premise or a status, something follows automatically.
branches.cn: 推理与资格：从一个前提或一种身份，某物自动随之而来。

branches.en: RESPECT: in legal prose the word can mark the aspect in which a statement holds.
branches.cn: 方面：在法律文体中，这个词可以标记一句话在哪个方面成立。

branches.en: RELATIVE USE: the archaic by which shows the compound doing a grammar job later taken by whereby.
branches.cn: 关系用法：古义的“凭借之”显示这个复合词曾承担后来由 whereby 接管的功能。

intro.en: Thereby has no derivational suffix. Its family is the there- compound set, built from there plus a preposition, and a few fixed academic patterns.
intro.cn: thereby 没有派生后缀。它的家族是 there- 复合词系列，由 there 加介词构成，另有若干固定的学术句式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source. Thereby is a native English compound of Old English þǣr and bī, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语来源。thereby 是古英语 þǣr 与 bī 构成的英语本土复合词，因此拉丁词条列表为空。

items.meaning: by that means or as a result of that
items.meaningCN: 借此；由此；从而（复合副词）
items.example: The ban cut traffic, thereby improving air quality.
items.exampleCN: 禁令减少了交通，从而改善了空气质量。

items.meaningCN: 凭借之；据此（关系复合词）
items.example: They agreed a process whereby disputes go to arbitration.
items.exampleCN: 他们商定了一个程序，据此争端提交仲裁。

items.example: The report and the tables therein are confidential.
items.exampleCN: 报告及其中表格均属机密。

items.example: The parties agreed to the terms and the annexes thereto.
items.exampleCN: 各方同意条款及所附附件。

items.example: The vote passed; thereupon the meeting closed.
items.exampleCN: 表决通过，会议随即结束。

items.example: He was satisfied therewith and signed.

items.meaning: the standard way of stating a result in academic prose
items.meaningCN: 学术写作中陈述结果的标准句式（thereby 后接现在分词）
items.example: The samples were sealed, thereby preventing evaporation.
items.exampleCN: 样品被密封，从而防止了蒸发。

items.meaning: a rarer pattern stating a consequence as a full clause
items.meaningCN: 较罕见的句式，用完整从句陈述后果
items.example: The treaty was signed, thereby the war ended.
items.exampleCN: 条约签署，战争由此结束。

items.meaning: there is a story attached to that fact
items.meaningCN: 这背后还有一段故事（固定文学短语）
items.example: He came by the map honestly; thereby hangs a tale.
items.exampleCN: 他得到那张地图来路正当；这背后还有一段故事。

items.meaning: thereby names the means, therefore names the inference
items.meaningCN: 对比用法：thereby 指手段，therefore 指推理
items.example: He lied, and therefore lost trust; he lied, thereby losing trust.
items.exampleCN: 他撒了谎，因此失去信任；他撒谎，从而失去了信任。

definition_zh: 织物；布料；结构；组织
definition_en: cloth made by weaving or knitting; the structure of a society or system; the way parts are joined
core_image: 经纬线交错织成的一大块布
scene: 这种织物摸起来很柔软。 This fabric feels very soft.
sceneCN: 这里 fabric 是「织物、布料」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这种织物摸起来很柔软。

senses.title: Woven cloth
senses.definition: cloth made by weaving or knitting threads
senses.definitionCN: 由纱线编织或针织成的布
senses.example: The curtains are made of cotton fabric.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘是用棉布做的。
senses.why: The core sense is material made from joined threads.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是由线交织而成的材料。

senses.title: Structure
senses.definition: the way the parts of something are joined together
senses.definitionCN: 事物各部分连接在一起的方式
senses.example: The fabric of the building is still strong.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋建筑的结构仍然坚固。
senses.why: Joined threads become joined parts.
senses.whyCN: 交织的线变成连接的结构。

senses.title: The social system
senses.definition: the basic structure of a society or group
senses.definitionCN: 社会或群体的基本结构
senses.example: Trust holds the social fabric together.
senses.exampleCN: 信任维系着社会结构。
senses.why: A woven surface becomes the web of society.
senses.whyCN: 织成的表面变成社会之网。

intro.en: Fabric comes from Latin fabrica, a workshop or craft, from faber, a worker.
intro.cn: fabric 来自拉丁语 fabrica（作坊、技艺），根源是 faber（工匠）。

items.en: Faber means a worker or craftsman.
items.cn: faber 意为工匠。

items.en: Fabrica means a workshop or craft.
items.cn: fabrica 意为作坊或技艺。

items.en: Fabricare means to make or build.
items.cn: fabricare 意为制作或建造。

items.en: Fabric reaches English through French.
items.cn: fabric 经法语进入英语。

items.en: Fabric means cloth and also a structure.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fabric 既指布料也指结构。

note.en: Fabric is cloth or structure; fabricate is to make up.
note.cn: fabric 是织物或结构，fabricate 则是制造或捏造。

entries.definition: to make or invent something
extremely good
a thin thread used in cloth
material made from threads
woven or knitted cloth
the way parts are arranged

normalIntro.en: Fabric is woven cloth and also the woven structure of a society.
normalIntro.cn: fabric 是织成的布，也指社会织成的结构。

normal.en: This fabric is soft and light.
normal.cn: 这种织物柔软轻便。

normal.en: The shop sells fabric by the meter.
normal.cn: 这家店按米卖布料。

normal.en: The old fabric of the city is changing.
normal.cn: 这座城市旧的结构正在改变。

normal.en: Poverty can damage the social fabric.
normal.cn: 贫困会损害社会结构。

normal.en: They chose a strong fabric for the curtains.
normal.cn: 他们为窗帘选了结实的布料。

abstract.en: Picture threads crossing over and under each other.
abstract.cn: 想象线一根根上下交错。

abstract.en: Imagine a city held together by many small ties.
abstract.cn: 想象城市被许多细小纽带连在一起。

abstract.en: Think of a net whose knots support the whole.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网，每个结都支撑整体。

examples.en: The dress is made from a light fabric.
examples.cn: 这条裙子用轻薄的布料做成。

examples.en: Trust is part of the fabric of a team.
examples.cn: 信任是团队结构的一部分。

examples.en: The fabric of the old house is still sound.
examples.cn: 老房子的结构仍然完好。

dict_mnemonic.text: fabric 与 fabricate 同源：先有「制作」，再指制作出的织物与结构。

root: 源自拉丁语 fabrica（作坊、技艺），由 faber（工匠）派生，核心义「制作出来的织物与结构」。

sensesIntro.en: Fabric means woven cloth, the way parts are joined, or the structure of a society.
sensesIntro.cn: fabric 意为织成的布、部件的连接方式，或社会结构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: threads woven into one strong sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：线交织成一整块结实的布。

branches.en: The base sense is woven cloth.
branches.cn: 基础义是织成的布。

branches.en: Joined threads become joined parts.
branches.cn: 交织的线变成连接的结构。

branches.en: A woven surface becomes the web of society.
branches.cn: 织成的表面变成社会之网。

branches.en: Cloth and building structure both depend on joining.
branches.cn: 布料与建筑结构都依赖连接。

branches.en: Material structure and social structure share a frame.
branches.cn: 物质结构与社会结构共享一个框架。

intro.en: Fabric belongs to the Latin faber family, like fabricate and fabrication.
intro.cn: fabric 属于拉丁语 faber 词族，与 fabricate、fabrication 同源。

latinIntro.en: Latin fabrica, fabricare, and faber are the source forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fabrica、fabricare 与 faber 是来源形式。

items.meaning: the act of making or inventing
items.example: The story was a complete fabrication.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事完全是捏造的。

items.meaning: a person who makes or invents things
items.example: The fabricator cut the metal sheets.

items.exampleCN: 他们坐在覆有织物的椅子上。

latinEntries.example: Faber is the worker behind fabrica.
latinEntries.exampleCN: faber 是 fabrica 背后的工匠。

definition_zh: 自信地；有把握地
definition_en: in a way that shows you are sure of yourself or of a result
core_image: 一个人走上讲台，脚步平稳，不回头看稿
scene: 她不用看稿，抬头把结论说了出来。 She answered the question confidently and clearly.
sceneCN: 这里 confidently 指「自信地」（第 1 个义项：以有把握的姿态）；句意是她自信而清楚地回答了问题。

senses.title: With a sure manner
senses.definition: in a manner that shows quiet belief in one's own ability
senses.definitionCN: 以对自己能力有平静信念的姿态
senses.example: She walked confidently onto the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 她自信地走上舞台。
senses.why: A steady step tells the room that the speaker belongs there.
senses.whyCN: 稳健的步伐告诉全场，讲话者属于这里。

senses.title: With firm expectation
senses.definition: in a way that shows certainty about a future result
senses.definitionCN: 以对将来结果有确定把握的方式
senses.example: They confidently predict a rise in sales.
senses.exampleCN: 他们有把握地预测销量会上升。
senses.why: A forecast stated without doubt asks others to trust the numbers behind it.
senses.whyCN: 毫无犹疑说出的预测，是在请别人相信背后的数据。

intro.en: Confidently is confident plus -ly, and confident goes back to Latin confidere, to trust completely.
intro.cn: confidently 由 confident 加 -ly 构成，而 confident 可追溯到拉丁语 confidere（完全信任）。

items.en: Fidere meant to trust, and confidere meant to trust without reserve.
items.cn: fidere 意为信任，confidere 意为毫无保留地信任。

items.en: Confidentia named the state of trusting fully.
items.cn: confidentia 指完全信任的状态。

items.en: French confident described a person sure of himself.
items.cn: 法语 confident 描述对自己有把握的人。

items.en: English confident entered use, and -ly soon turned it into an adverb.
items.cn: 英语 confident 进入使用，随后 -ly 把它变成副词。

items.en: Confidently now describes both a manner and a firm expectation.
items.cn: 如今 confidently 既描述姿态，也描述坚定的预期。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the family words that most often get mixed with confidently, and the meaning group names other adverbs of assurance.
note.cn: 形近组收的是最容易与 confidently 混淆的同族词，近义组列出其他表示有把握的副词。

entries.definition: sure about one's own ability
meant to be kept secret
a person trusted with private matters
in a way that shows no doubt
in a strong and steady way
in a brave and unafraid way

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a steady walk to a stage, then move to a clear answer and to a bold forecast.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从稳步走向舞台开始，再走到清楚的回答与大胆的预测。

normal.en: Confident plus -ly turns the adjective into the way you do it.
normal.cn: confident 加 -ly，就把形容词变成做事的姿态。

normal.en: Speak confidently and the room leans in a little.
normal.cn: 自信地讲话，整个房间都会微微前倾。

normal.en: Walking confidently is mostly a matter of not checking the floor.
normal.cn: 自信地走路，多半就是不去盯着地面看。

normal.en: A confidently made prediction is one with numbers behind it.
normal.cn: 有把握的预测，背后一定站着数字。

normal.en: The adverb never adds the confidence; it only shows it.
normal.cn: 副词不会添加自信，它只是把自信显示出来。

abstract.en: Picture a chin held level and a gaze kept forward.
abstract.cn: 想象下巴端平、目光一直向前。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that does not search for a pen.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手不再到处找笔。

abstract.en: Picture a voice that lands on the last word.
abstract.cn: 想象一个把最后一字稳稳说完的声音。

examples.en: She confidently told the class what she had found.
examples.cn: 她自信地告诉全班自己发现了什么。

examples.en: He confidently walked to the front of the hall.
examples.cn: 他自信地走到大厅前方。

examples.en: The report confidently predicts a recovery next year.
examples.cn: 这份报告有把握地预测明年将会复苏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confidently 记成 confident（自信的）加 ly：用自信的样子做一件事，就是自信地。

root: 由 confident 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，而 confident 源自拉丁语 confidere（com 完全 + fidere 信任），词义为自信地、有把握地。

sensesIntro.en: From the calm manner of a person who trusts himself, to the firm tone of a forecast.
sensesIntro.cn: 从相信自己之人那份平静姿态，到一份预测里坚定的语气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steady step, a level chin, and a voice that ends cleanly.
core.cn: 核心意象：稳健的一步、端平的下巴、干净利落收尾的声音。

branches.en: The manner sense is about how the body carries quiet trust.
branches.cn: 姿态义项讲的是身体如何承载平静的信任。

branches.en: The expectation sense is about how firmly a result is stated.
branches.cn: 预期义项讲的是结果被说得多确定。

branches.en: Both senses need a voice without hesitation.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要一个不迟疑的声音。

branches.en: Confidence shown is often more convincing than confidence claimed.
branches.cn: 表现出来的自信，通常比声称的自信更有说服力。

branches.en: Confidently predicting is a promise that evidence will carry.
branches.cn: 有把握地预测，是承诺证据会撑住这句话。

intro.en: Confidently is the adjective confident plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: confidently 是形容词 confident 加上副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The Latin trust base fid- also appears in fidelity and confide.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的信任词基 fid- 也出现在 fidelity 与 confide 中。

items.meaning: in a sure and steady way
items.example: She spoke confidently to the crowd.
He is confident about the match.
Her confidence is easy to see.
items.exampleCN: 她的自信一眼就能看出。

items.meaning: to trust someone with a secret
a person trusted with private things
with too much belief in oneself
items.exampleCN: 他过于自信地跳过了训练。

items.example: The team is known for its fidelity.

definition_zh: 容忍；忍受；容许；对……有耐受力
definition_en: to allow something you dislike to happen or exist without protest, or to endure something painful or unpleasant
core_image: 双手按住桌沿，任由对面的人大声说话，始终没有起身离开
scene: 会议室里有人把空调开得很低，靠窗的同事只把外套披上，一言不发。 She can tolerate the cold office far better than a heated argument.
sceneCN: 这里 tolerate 是「忍受」（第 2 个义项：忍受不适）；句意为她对寒冷的办公室的忍受力远胜于对一场激烈争吵的忍受力。画面里有冷气口、外套与沉默的同事。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ance 构成名词，义为「宽容；忍耐力；公差」
由动词加 -ant 构成形容词，义为「宽容的」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可忍受的；尚可的」
由动词加 -ation 构成，义为「容许；信仰宽容」

senses.title: To allow what one dislikes
senses.definition: to let something happen or exist although one disapproves of it
senses.definitionCN: 虽然不赞成，仍让某事发生或存在
senses.example: The teacher will not tolerate cheating in any form.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老师不容忍任何形式的作弊。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to bear, and letting an unwanted thing stay is the everyday shape of bearing it.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为承担，让不想要的东西留在身边，就是「承担」的日常形态。

senses.title: To endure discomfort
senses.definition: to put up with pain, heat, noise, or another unpleasant condition
senses.definitionCN: 忍受疼痛、高温、噪音或其他不适条件
senses.example: Few plants can tolerate this salt-laden soil.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有植物能忍受这种含盐的土壤。
senses.why: The physical sense of carrying a burden is still visible here: the body holds the discomfort without giving way.
senses.whyCN: 背负重物的身体感在这里仍然可见：身体撑住不适而不垮。

senses.title: To bear a person
senses.definition: to accept a difficult person without breaking the relationship
senses.definitionCN: 接受一个难相处的人而不把关系弄僵
senses.example: He tolerated his uncle's teasing throughout the whole dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 整顿晚饭他都容忍着叔叔的取笑。
senses.why: Bearing a weight and bearing a person are the same effort of self-control in Latin idiom.
senses.whyCN: 在拉丁语习惯里，承担重量与承担一个人是同一份自制的力。

senses.title: To accept a substance safely
senses.definition: of the body, to take a drug or food without harm
senses.definitionCN: 指身体能服用药物或食物而不受伤害
senses.example: Some patients cannot tolerate penicillin and need another drug.
senses.exampleCN: 有些病人不能耐受青霉素，需要换一种药。
senses.why: A body that lets a substance remain inside without damage is bearing it in the strictest sense.
senses.whyCN: 身体让某种物质留在体内而不受损，正是最严格意义上的承受。

senses.title: To permit by law or custom
senses.definition: to permit an activity officially or by long custom
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或长期习俗上准许某项活动
senses.example: The old city tolerates street musicians in the square until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老城容许街头乐手在广场演奏到午夜。
senses.why: When the bearing hand is a whole community, tolerating becomes a licence rather than a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 当承受者是整个共同体，容忍就由心情变成了许可。

senses.title: To survive under difficult conditions
senses.definition: of a plant or animal, to survive and grow in a harsh environment
senses.definitionCN: 指动植物在恶劣环境中存活生长
senses.example: These shrubs tolerate drought and poor soil better than any grass.
senses.exampleCN: 这些灌木比任何草类都更能耐受干旱与贫瘠的土壤。
senses.why: Surviving a hard environment is bearing it for a lifetime, so the word moves from feeling to biology.
senses.whyCN: 在严酷环境中活下来，就是把环境承受一辈子，于是这个词从感受走向生物。

senses.title: To accept without correcting
senses.definition: to let an error or fault pass unnoticed or uncorrected
senses.definitionCN: 让错误或过失被忽视、不加纠正
senses.example: The editor tolerated a few awkward lines in an otherwise strong report.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑默许了这篇总体有力的报告里几处生硬的句子。
senses.why: Here the bearing is quiet: nothing is approved, but nothing is stopped either.
senses.whyCN: 这里的承受是无声的：既没有认可，也没有阻止。

senses.title: To hold evidence without rejecting it
senses.definition: in measurement, to allow results to fall within an accepted range
senses.definitionCN: 在测量中允许结果落在可接受的范围内
senses.example: The instrument can tolerate a drift of two degrees before a reading is discarded.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器能容许两度的漂移，超出才作废读数。
senses.why: The engineering notion of a permissible margin is the technical child of the old verb for bearing.
senses.whyCN: 工程上「允许的范围」这一概念，就是「承受」这个老动词的现代技术后代。

intro.en: Tolerate is the English verb formed on Latin tolerare, to bear; the deeper origin of the Latin word is uncertain and competing explanations have been offered.
intro.cn: tolerate 是在拉丁语 tolerare（承担、忍受）基础上形成的英语动词；这个词的更深来源不确定，学界有几种互相竞争的解释。

items.en: Tolerare means to bear up under a burden, and Roman writers use it for enduring pain, work, and difficult people.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tolerare 意为在重负下撑住，罗马作家用它表示忍受疼痛、劳苦与难缠的人。

items.en: The past participle toleratus and the adjective tolerabilis are common in classical prose.
items.cn: 过去分词 toleratus 与形容词 tolerabilis 在古典散文中很常见。

items.en: The link to ferre, to carry, is sometimes proposed, but the etymology is generally marked as uncertain.
items.cn: 有人提出它与表示「携带」的 ferre 有关，但词源一般被标为不确定。

items.en: English forms tolerate in the sixteenth century, first in the physical sense and soon in the moral one.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪构成 tolerate，先用于身体方面，很快扩展到道德方面。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the verb is used of religious and political forbearance.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，这个动词用于宗教与政治上的宽容。

items.en: In the nineteenth century medicine and engineering give the word its senses of drug tolerance and permitted error.
items.cn: 十九世纪，医学与工程学赋予它药物耐受与允许误差的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun and adjective of the same family, while the near-meaning group places the verb among words for putting up with and for allowing.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一词族的名词与形容词，近义组则把这个动词放进「忍受」与「容许」的语义场。

entries.definition: the quality of being willing to accept differences
willing to accept what one dislikes
bearable, not too bad
the practice of allowing beliefs one dislikes
to suffer something painful for a long time
to accept something annoying without complaining
to accept wrong behaviour as if it were acceptable
to order that something must not happen

normalIntro.en: These memories build on the Latin verb, on the suffixes, and on the way the word moves from feelings to machines.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从拉丁动词、后缀构词以及这个词由感受走向机器的路径入手。

normal.en: Tolerare is to carry, so to tolerate is to carry something you would rather put down.
normal.cn: tolerare 是扛，所以 tolerate 就是扛着一件你更想放下的东西。

normal.en: Tolerance, tolerant, tolerable all share the stem; only the endings change the part of speech.
normal.cn: tolerance、tolerant、tolerable 共用一个词干，只是词尾改变了词性。

normal.en: Cannot tolerate is the standard negative, and the modal shows that bearing has a limit.
normal.cn: cannot tolerate 是标准否定式，情态动词说明承受是有上限的。

normal.en: Plants that tolerate salt are said to be salt-tolerant, a compound made from the adjective.
normal.cn: 耐盐的植物被称为 salt-tolerant，这个词是用形容词构成的复合词。

normal.en: In a lab, an instrument tolerates drift, which links the verb to the idea of a permitted margin.
normal.cn: 在实验室里，仪器容忍漂移，这把这个动词和「允许的余量」联系起来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a hot cup that stays there one more second than it wants to.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手握着烫杯，比它想握的时间多坚持了一秒。

abstract.en: Think of a bridge that bends a little in the wind instead of breaking, and that bending is tolerance.
abstract.cn: 想一座在风里略微弯曲而不折断的桥，那一点弯曲就是承受。

abstract.en: To tolerate is to leave the door unlocked for a guest you do not entirely trust.
abstract.cn: 容忍就是给一个你并不完全信任的客人留一扇没锁的门。

examples.en: We do not tolerate bullying in this club.
examples.cn: 在这个社团里我们不容忍欺凌。

examples.en: The workers tolerated the heat until the fans were repaired.
examples.cn: 工人们一直忍受着高温，直到风扇被修好。

examples.en: Certain grasses tolerate salt water better than others.
examples.cn: 有些草类比其他草类更能耐受咸水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「托了忍特」——托着、忍着，还特别能忍，就是容忍、忍受。

root: 拉丁语 tolerare（承担、忍受），同族名词 tolerantia、形容词 tolerabilis。词根更深来源不确定，一般认为与表示「举起、支撑」一类词形有关，但无定论。

sensesIntro.en: The entry runs from allowing an unwelcome act through enduring discomfort, bearing a difficult person, surviving a substance or a climate, and finally tolerating error in law and in instruments.
sensesIntro.cn: 本词从容许不受欢迎的行为，经忍受不适、容忍难缠的人、耐受某种物质或气候，最后到法律与仪器上容许误差。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: carrying a weight and choosing not to drop it.
core.cn: 核心意象：扛着重量，选择不放下。

branches.en: Allowing what one dislikes to continue.
branches.cn: 让不喜欢的继续存在。

branches.en: Bearing discomfort and difficult people.
branches.cn: 忍受不适与难相处的人。

branches.en: Bearing a substance in the body.
branches.cn: 身体承受某种物质。

branches.en: Allowing by law or custom.
branches.cn: 在法律或习俗上准许。

branches.en: Surviving a hard environment or a measured margin.
branches.cn: 在严酷环境或可量度的误差中存活。

intro.en: The verb is a Latin stem with the verb ending -ate, and the family is completed with -ance, -ant, -able, and -ation.
intro.cn: 这个动词是拉丁词干加动词词尾 -ate，同族词由 -ance、-ant、-able 与 -ation 补全。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the verb and its near relatives that English borrowed or refashioned.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条给出英语借入或改形的动词及其近亲。

items.example: The stem is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干是整个词族的基础。

items.example: Tolerate is built with this ending.
Toleration is the older noun for the practice.
items.exampleCN: toleration 是表示这种做法的老名词。
tolerating 可以引导修饰短语。

definition_zh: 不新鲜的；陈旧的；走味的
definition_en: no longer fresh, or no longer interesting because it is too familiar
core_image: 一块放久了变硬的面包
scene: 面包放久变硬了。 The bread has gone stale.
sceneCN: 这里 stale 是「不新鲜的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：面包放久变硬了。

senses.title: Not fresh
senses.definition: no longer fresh, especially of food
senses.definitionCN: 尤指食物不再新鲜
senses.example: The bread has gone stale.
senses.exampleCN: 面包放久变硬了。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的物理义项。

senses.title: Old and dull
senses.definition: no longer interesting because it is too familiar
senses.definitionCN: 因过于熟悉而不再有趣
senses.example: His jokes are getting stale.
senses.exampleCN: 他的笑话越来越老套。
senses.why: Food going stale became ideas going dull.
senses.whyCN: 食物变味，引申为想法乏味。

senses.title: Without life
senses.definition: flat or lifeless, as of air or a performance
senses.definitionCN: 指空气或表演沉闷、缺乏生气
senses.example: The room was full of stale air.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里满是污浊的空气。
senses.why: Staleness can be felt without taste.
senses.whyCN: 「不新鲜」不靠尝也能感觉到。

intro.en: Stale comes from Old French estale, fixed or standing, of uncertain deeper origin.
intro.cn: stale 来自古法语 estale（固定不动的），更早来源不确定。

items.en: The deeper origin is not certain.
items.cn: 更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Estale meant fixed or settled.
items.cn: estale 意为固定的、停滞的。

items.en: Stale described drink or food gone flat.
items.cn: stale 描述走味的饮料或食物。

items.en: The sense widened to anything old.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何陈旧之物。

items.en: Stale jokes and stale air both became common.
items.cn: 「老掉牙的笑话」和「污浊的空气」都成了常见说法。

note.en: Stale is compared with look-alike words and words for old or dry.
note.cn: 把 stale 与形近词以及表示陈旧或干燥的词作比较。

entries.definition: a post or a share
a small open shop
a country or condition
having existed for a long time
without moisture
not interesting

normalIntro.en: Stale means time has taken the freshness out of food, air, or jokes.
normalIntro.cn: stale 指时间抽走了食物、空气或笑话里的新鲜感。

normal.en: This bread is stale.
normal.cn: 这面包不新鲜了。

normal.en: Open a window; the air is stale.
normal.cn: 开扇窗吧，空气太闷了。

normal.en: The joke felt stale.
normal.cn: 那个笑话显得老套。

normal.en: Their marriage had gone stale.
normal.cn: 他们的婚姻已失去活力。

normal.en: Stale smoke hung in the room.
normal.cn: 陈腐的烟味滞留在房间里。

abstract.en: Even honey loses its shine in time.
abstract.cn: 再甜的蜜，也会随时间失去光泽。

abstract.en: Repetition turns wonder into habit.
abstract.cn: 重复把惊奇变成习惯。

abstract.en: Freshness is a guest, not a resident.
abstract.cn: 新鲜是客人，不是常住户。

examples.en: The bread has gone stale.
examples.cn: 面包放久变硬了。

examples.en: His jokes are getting stale.
examples.cn: 他的笑话越来越老套。

examples.en: The room was full of stale air.
examples.cn: 房间里满是污浊的空气。

dict_mnemonic.text: stale 是「不新鲜的、陈旧的」；stale bread 是不新鲜的面包，stale air 是污浊的空气，go stale 是变味、变陈旧。

root: 来自古法语 estale（固定不动的），更早来源不确定；由「停滞不动」引申为食物走味、空气沉闷、想法陈旧。

sensesIntro.en: Stale means no longer fresh, old and dull, or flat and lifeless.
sensesIntro.cn: stale 指不再新鲜、陈旧乏味，或沉闷无生气。

core.en: Freshness lost through time.
core.cn: 被时间带走的新鲜感。

branches.en: A loaf hardens on the shelf.
branches.cn: 面包在架子上变硬。

branches.en: A familiar joke draws no laugh.
branches.cn: 熟悉的笑话引不来笑声。

branches.en: Closed windows keep the room heavy.
branches.cn: 关着的窗让房间沉闷。

branches.en: Food and humour both lose their edge.
branches.cn: 食物与幽默，都会失去锋芒。

branches.en: What is repeated becomes airless.
branches.cn: 被重复的东西，会变得不透气。

intro.en: Stale forms comparisons, an adverb, and a noun.
intro.cn: stale 构成比较级、副词和名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word came through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，经古法语传入。

items.example: That is the stalest joke here.
items.exampleCN: 那是这里最老套的笑话。
那句话被陈腐地重复着。

items.example: The staleness of the air was clear.
They fed stale bread to the birds.
items.exampleCN: 他们把不新鲜的面包喂鸟。

definition_zh: 爪子；脚掌；用手抓摸
definition_en: the foot of an animal that has claws, especially a cat or dog; also to touch or scrape something with such a foot
core_image: 一只毛茸茸的脚掌落下，爪尖在触地前才微微伸出
scene: 清晨的厨房门外，一只橘猫蹲在垫子上，盯着关紧的门。 The cat lifted one paw and tapped the wood.
sceneCN: 这里是「爪子」（第 1 个义项：动物的脚掌）；句意为猫抬起一只爪子去拍木门。图中可辨识物件：橘猫、门缝、门口的地垫。

derivatives.zh: 由 paw 与 print 复合而成，指动物踩在软地面上留下的爪印
由 paw 加 -ing 构成的动名词，指用爪子反复抓扒的动作

senses.title: The foot of a clawed animal
senses.definition: the foot of an animal such as a cat or dog, with soft pads and claws
senses.definitionCN: 猫、狗等动物带软垫和爪尖的脚掌
senses.example: The cat lifted one paw and tapped the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 猫抬起一只爪子拍了拍木门。
senses.why: The word names the whole padded foot rather than a single claw, which is why it covers the part that walks and the part that grips.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指整只带肉垫的脚掌，而不是单根爪尖，所以既能说走路的那部分，也能说抓握的那部分。

senses.title: A person's hand, informally
senses.definition: a person's hand, used in informal speech, often when the hand is clumsy or intrusive
senses.definitionCN: 口语里指人的手，常带笨拙或乱伸的意味
senses.example: Keep your paws off my notes.
senses.exampleCN: 别用你的手碰我的笔记。
senses.why: Calling a hand a paw borrows the animal foot to suggest clumsiness or greed, so the same word slides from beast to person.
senses.whyCN: 把人的手叫作爪子，是借动物的脚掌暗示笨拙或贪心，于是同一个词从兽类滑到人身上。

senses.title: To scrape with a paw
senses.definition: to touch, scrape or hit something repeatedly with a paw
senses.definitionCN: 用爪子反复触碰、刮擦或拍打某物
senses.example: The dog pawed at the door until someone opened it.
senses.exampleCN: 狗一直扒门，直到有人把它打开。
senses.why: From the noun for the foot comes a verb for what that foot does, and the repeated scraping is the action most often attached to it.
senses.whyCN: 名词指脚掌，动词就指这只脚做的事，而最常与它相连的动作就是反复刮擦。

senses.title: To touch someone roughly
senses.definition: to touch a person in a rough or unwanted way, especially with the hands
senses.definitionCN: 用手粗鲁地或不被欢迎地触碰别人
senses.example: He pawed at her sleeve to get her attention.
senses.exampleCN: 他粗鲁地扯她的袖子想引起注意。
senses.why: Because a paw is clumsy and has no fine control, the verb came to describe hands that grab without care, and the meaning turns negative.
senses.whyCN: 爪子笨拙、没有细致控制，动词便用来形容不加分寸乱抓的手，含义也转向负面。

intro.en: The word for an animal foot appears in Middle English, and the usual account traces it to an Old French form; anything earlier is uncertain.
intro.cn: 表示动物脚掌的这个词见于中古英语，通常认为来自古法语的一种形式；再往前的情况并不确定。

items.en: Old French patte meant the foot or paw of an animal, and it is generally taken as the source of the English word.
items.cn: 古法语 patte 意为动物的脚或爪子，一般认为这就是英语这个词的来源。

items.en: Some scholars connect it with Germanic words for a foot, perhaps through Frankish, but this remains a reconstructed and disputed suggestion.
items.cn: 一些学者把它与日耳曼语中表示「脚」的词联系起来，可能经由法兰克语，但这仍属于重构且有争议的推测。

items.en: Middle English records pawe in the fourteenth century, spelled with a w that later settled into the modern form.
items.cn: 中古英语在十四世纪记录了 pawe 这一写法，词尾的 w 后来固定成现代形式。

items.en: Early modern writers extended the noun to a person's hand in rough or joking speech, and the verb for scraping followed.
items.cn: 近代早期作家在粗俗或玩笑的语气里把这个名词扩展到人的手，表示抓扒的动词也随之出现。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the animal sense and the informal human sense, and forms compounds such as pawprint for the mark left behind.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留动物义与口语中的人手义，并造出 pawprint 这类复合词，指留下的印记。

note.en: The look-alike group holds compounds and inflections of the word plus one short word that merely shares its ending; the near-meaning group holds other words for feet and for grasping.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的复合形式与变形，以及一个只是词尾相同的短词；近义组收其他表示脚掌与抓握的词。

entries.definition: The mark a paw leaves on soft ground or on a dusty floor.
entries.definitionCN: 爪子在软地或落灰的地面上留下的印记。

entries.definition: The plural of the noun and the third person singular of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数，也是动词的第三人称单数形式。

entries.definition: A bone of the mouth used for biting; only the ending looks alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 嘴里用来咬东西的骨；只是词尾相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: A sharp curved nail on the foot of a bird or animal.
entries.definitionCN: 鸟或动物脚上弯曲而锋利的甲。

entries.definition: The soft part on the underside of an animal's foot.
entries.definitionCN: 动物脚掌下面柔软的肉垫部分。

entries.definition: The hard horny foot of a horse, cow or similar animal.
entries.definitionCN: 马、牛等动物坚硬而角质化的脚。

entries.definition: The part of the body at the end of the arm, with fingers.
entries.definitionCN: 手臂末端带手指的部分。

normalIntro.en: With no reliable Latin root, the word is best held by its French source, its English spellings, and the small family built from it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁词根，最好靠它的法语来源、英语拼写，以及由它组成的小词族来记。

normal.en: Old French patte meant an animal's foot, and English took the shape of that word as paw.
normal.cn: 古法语 patte 意为动物的脚，英语照这个词的形状收下了 paw。

normal.en: Add s and you get paws, which is both the plural noun and the third person singular verb.
normal.cn: 加上 s 成为 paws，既是名词复数，也是动词的第三人称单数。

normal.en: Paw at the door describes the scraping motion a cat makes when it wants to be let in.
normal.cn: paw at the door 描写猫想进屋时用爪子刮门的样子。

normal.en: Pawprint joins paw and print, so the mark is literally the print of a paw.
normal.cn: pawprint 把 paw 与 print 拼在一起，那印记字面上就是爪子的印。

normal.en: A cat's paw in a story is a person used by someone else to do a risky job.
normal.cn: 故事里的 cat's paw 指被人利用去干冒险差事的人。

abstract.en: A paw is a foot that still remembers hunting, which is why the same word can mean standing and grabbing.
abstract.cn: 爪子是一只还记得捕猎的脚，所以同一个词既能表示站立，也能表示抓取。

abstract.en: Calling a human hand a paw is a small insult: it says the hand has lost its delicacy.
abstract.cn: 把人的手叫作爪子是一句小小的贬损：它在说这只手已经失去了细致。

abstract.en: The soft pad under the animal's foot is a cushion that also hides the claws until they are needed.
abstract.cn: 动物脚掌下那块软垫既是缓冲，也把爪尖藏到需要时才亮出来。

examples.en: The cat lifted one paw and tapped the wood.
examples.cn: 猫抬起一只爪子拍了拍木门。

examples.en: Muddy paw prints covered the kitchen floor.
examples.cn: 泥爪印布满了厨房地面。

examples.en: The dog pawed at the door until someone opened it.
examples.cn: 狗一直扒门，直到有人把它打开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「刨」——猫用爪子在门上刨来刨去；paw 就是爪子，也是用爪抓。

root: 一般认为来自古法语 patte（动物的脚、爪）；更早来源不确定，有学者把它与日耳曼语中表示「脚」的词相联系，属重构假说；无可靠拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a soft padded foot that both carries the body and scrapes at what it wants; the human and rough-touching senses grow from that same clumsiness.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是既能承重、又会抓扒的带垫脚掌；指人手与粗鲁触碰的两个义项，都从这种笨拙里长出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft padded foot pressing down, claws folded until the moment they are needed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只带肉垫的脚掌按下去，爪尖折着，等到需要时才伸出。

branches.en: a cat waiting at a closed door
branches.cn: 一只猫等在关着的门边

branches.en: a hand pushed away from a desk
branches.cn: 一只手被人从桌边挡开

branches.en: claws working at wood until it gives
branches.cn: 爪尖一直刮到木头松动

branches.en: a sleeve pulled without asking
branches.cn: 没有打招呼就扯住的袖子

branches.en: the same foot that stands also scratches
branches.cn: 同一只脚既站着，也用来抓扒

intro.en: This word has no reliable Latin root, so its build is held by the Old French form, two English spellings, and the compounding and suffixing that follow.
intro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁词根，构词线索由古法语形式、两个英语拼写，以及随后的复合与加缀组成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; the trail stops at Old French and possibly a Germanic source.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词：线索止于古法语，再往前可能是某种日耳曼语来源。

items.meaning: the mark left by a paw
a mark pressed onto a surface
the act of scraping with paws

definition_zh: 展出；陈列；表现出；展品
definition_en: to show something in public, to show a quality or symptom, or an object on display
core_image: 玻璃柜里的一件展品
scene: 博物馆展出了几件唐代陶器。 The museum exhibited several Tang pottery pieces.
sceneCN: 这里 exhibit 是「展出、陈列」（第 1 个义项）；句意：博物馆展出了几件唐代陶器。

senses.title: Show in public
senses.definition: to show something in a public place for people to see
senses.definitionCN: 在公共场所陈列某物供人观看
senses.example: The gallery exhibits local paintings.
senses.exampleCN: 这家画廊展出本地画作。
senses.why: The object is held out for the public eye.
senses.whyCN: 物品被举到公众眼前。

senses.title: Show a sign
senses.definition: to show a feeling, quality, or symptom
senses.definitionCN: 表现出某种情感、特质或症状
senses.example: The patient exhibited no signs of fever.
senses.exampleCN: 病人没有表现出发烧的迹象。
senses.why: An inner state is held out where others can see it.
senses.whyCN: 内在状态被展示出来让人看见。

senses.title: Displayed object
senses.definition: an object shown in a museum or public show
senses.definitionCN: 在博物馆或公开展览中陈列的物品
senses.example: The gold mask is the finest exhibit here.
senses.exampleCN: 这件金面具是这里最精美的展品。
senses.why: The noun names the thing that is held out.
senses.whyCN: 名词指被展示出来的那件东西。

intro.en: Exhibit comes from Latin exhibere, to hold out.
intro.cn: exhibit 源自拉丁语 exhibere，意为向外持有、呈出。

items.en: Habere means to have or hold.
items.cn: habere 意为拥有、持有。

items.en: Exhibere joins ex-, out, with habere, to hold.
items.cn: exhibere 由 ex-（出）与 habere（持有）组成。

items.en: Exhibere means to present or display.
items.cn: exhibere 意为呈出、展示。

items.en: English exhibit keeps the public display sense.
items.cn: 英语 exhibit 保留公开展示的含义。

items.en: Exhibit also becomes a noun for a displayed object.
items.cn: exhibit 又变成名词，指陈列的物件。

note.en: Exhibit holds an object out; inhibit holds a person back.
note.cn: exhibit 把东西举出来，inhibit 则把人拦住。

entries.definition: a public show of objects
a person or firm that shows goods
to stop or slow something
to put something where it can be seen
to let something be seen
to offer something for viewing

normalIntro.en: Exhibit holds an object or a sign out for others.
normalIntro.cn: exhibit 把物品或迹象举出来给人看。

normal.en: The museum exhibits ancient tools.
normal.cn: 博物馆展出古代工具。

normal.en: The patient exhibited a mild cough.
normal.cn: 病人表现出轻微咳嗽。

normal.en: The gold mask is a famous exhibit.
normal.cn: 金面具是一件著名展品。

normal.en: Local artists exhibit at the hall each spring.
normal.cn: 本地艺术家每年春天在大厅展出。

normal.en: The painting is on exhibit until June.
normal.cn: 这幅画展出到六月。

abstract.en: Picture an object under a glass case.
abstract.cn: 想象一件放在玻璃柜里的物品。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand holding a card up to a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把卡片举向人群。

abstract.en: Think of a face that shows a hidden mood.
abstract.cn: 想象一张显露内心情绪的脸。

examples.en: The fair exhibits tools from many countries.
examples.cn: 博览会展出许多国家的工具。

examples.en: Her face exhibited no sign of fear.
examples.cn: 她脸上没有露出恐惧的迹象。

examples.en: The small exhibit drew a large crowd.
examples.cn: 这件小展品吸引了大批观众。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ hibit（持有）」——把东西拿到外面举着，就是展出；把情绪摆在脸上，就是表现出。

root: 拉丁语 exhibere（向外呈出）＝ ex-（出）＋ habere（持有）→ exhibit，核心义「拿出去给人看」。

sensesIntro.en: Exhibit means to show something in public, to show a quality or symptom, or an object on display.
sensesIntro.cn: exhibit 意为公开展出、表现出某种特质或症状，或陈列的展品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object in a glass case.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃柜里的一件展品。

branches.en: Public showing is the core sense.
branches.cn: 公开展出是核心义项。

branches.en: Feelings and symptoms are also held out.
branches.cn: 情感与症状同样被展示出来。

branches.en: The noun names the object shown.
branches.cn: 名词指被展示的物品。

branches.en: The act and the object belong together.
branches.cn: 展出行为与展品相互依存。

branches.en: Both senses put something in view.
branches.cn: 两者都把某物放到视野中。

intro.en: Exhibit combines ex-, out, with Latin habere, to hold.
intro.cn: exhibit 由 ex-（出）与拉丁语 habere（持有）组成。

latinIntro.en: Exhibere gives exhibitio and then English exhibit.
latinIntro.cn: exhibere 给出 exhibitio，再到英语 exhibit。

items.exampleCN: exhibit 保留举出展示的意象。
exhibitor 加上了表示人的词尾。

latinEntries.example: Exhibere is the source of exhibit.
latinEntries.exampleCN: exhibere 是 exhibit 的来源。

definition_zh: 平等；相等；均等
definition_en: the state of being equal in rights, status, or amount
core_image: 天平两端准确齐平，谁也不少一分
scene: 法律保证男女在就业上享有平等。 The law guarantees equality between men and women at work.
sceneCN: 这里 equality 是「平等」（第 1 个义项：在权利或地位上相同）；句意：法律保证男女在就业上享有平等。

senses.title: Equal rights and status
senses.definition: the state in which people have the same rights, opportunities, and respect
senses.definitionCN: 人们拥有相同权利、机会与尊重的情形
senses.example: The movement fought for equality in education.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动为教育平等而斗争。
senses.why: The noun adds -ity to equal, naming the state of being level and fair.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由 equal 加 -ity 构成，指齐平而公平的状态。

senses.title: Equality in amount or value
senses.definition: the condition of being the same in size, amount, or value
senses.definitionCN: 在大小、数量或价值上相同的状况
senses.example: The treaty rests on the equality of the two sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约建立在双方对等的基础上。
senses.why: Before it meant fair treatment, the word simply named an even balance.
senses.whyCN: 在表示公平对待之前，这个词只表示均衡。

senses.title: Evenness of treatment
senses.definition: the quality of treating all cases by the same standard
senses.definitionCN: 以同一标准对待所有情况的品质
senses.example: Judges must show equality to every citizen.
senses.exampleCN: 法官必须对每位公民一视同仁。
senses.why: A level balance in practice becomes consistent and impartial treatment.
senses.whyCN: 均衡在实际中表现为一致而公正的对待。

intro.en: Equality comes from Latin aequalitas, evenness, from aequalis, equal, and aequus, level.
intro.cn: equality 来自拉丁语 aequalitas（均匀、相等），源于 aequalis（相等的）与 aequus（平的）。

items.en: Aequus means level or fair.
items.cn: aequus 意为平的、公平的。

items.en: Aequalis means uniform or equal.
items.cn: aequalis 意为均匀的、相等的。

items.en: Aequalitas names the state of being equal.
items.cn: aequalitas 指相等的状态。

items.en: Equal brings the adjective into French and English.
items.cn: equal 把这个形容词带入法语和英语。

items.en: Modern English adds -ity to form the noun equality.
items.cn: 现代英语加 -ity 构成名词 equality。

note.en: Equality is the state noun of equal, close to its family and to words for fairness.
note.cn: equality 是 equal 的状态名词，与自身词族以及表示公平的词相邻。

entries.definition: the same in amount or status
in an equal way
to treat as equal
just and equal treatment
the state of being equal in rank
fairness in the way people are treated

normalIntro.en: Equality is the state of the equal: a level scale applied to people and to numbers.
normalIntro.cn: equality 是 equal 的状态：把水平的天平用于人与数字。

normal.en: Gender equality means equal chances for women and men.
normal.cn: gender equality 指男女机会平等。

normal.en: Equality before the law means the law treats everyone alike.
normal.cn: equality before the law 指法律对人人一视同仁。

normal.en: The adjective equal and the noun equality differ by only a suffix.
normal.cn: 形容词 equal 与名词 equality 只差一个词尾。

normal.en: Equality of opportunity is a common political phrase.
normal.cn: equality of opportunity 是常见的政治短语。

normal.en: Compare fairness: fairness stresses justice, equality stresses sameness.
normal.cn: 对比 fairness：fairness 强调公正，equality 强调相同。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with both pans at the very same height.
abstract.cn: 想象天平的托盘处在完全相同的高度。

abstract.en: Imagine two doors of exactly the same width.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇宽度完全相同的门。

abstract.en: Think of a line drawn straight through the middle of a page.
abstract.cn: 想象页面正中画着一条笔直的线。

examples.en: They marched for equality and justice.
examples.cn: 他们为平等与正义而游行。

examples.en: True equality means the same rules for everyone.
examples.cn: 真正的平等意味着人人适用同样的规则。

examples.en: The two countries agreed on the equality of their trade rights.
examples.cn: 两国就贸易权利对等达成一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equal + ity」——给「相等」加上状态名词尾巴，就是「平等」；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（平的、公平的）→ aequalis（相等的）→ aequalitas（相等状态）→ 英语 equality，核心义「彼此齐平的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Equality first names fair rights, then an even balance of amount, and then consistent treatment.
sensesIntro.cn: equality 先指公平权利，再指数额上的均衡，最后指一致对待。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale whose two sides sit at the same height.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两边处在同一高度。

branches.en: Fair rights are the central social sense.
branches.cn: 公平权利是核心社会义项。

branches.en: Even amount is the measurable sense.
branches.cn: 数额相等是可测量的义项。

branches.en: Consistent treatment applies balance to practice.
branches.cn: 一致对待把平衡用于实践。

branches.en: Equal rights require the same standard for all.
branches.cn: 平等权利要求对所有人使用同一标准。

branches.en: Both fair shares and fair rights rest on an even balance.
branches.cn: 公平分配与公平权利都建立在均衡之上。

intro.en: Equality is a Latin state noun built on aequus, with the suffix -ity added in English.
intro.cn: equality 是建立在 aequus 之上的拉丁状态名词，英语中加入词尾 -ity。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus means level, and aequalitas means evenness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为平的，aequalitas 意为均匀、相等。

items.example: Aequalitas is the direct Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: aequalitas 是直接的拉丁语名词。

definition_zh: 种族的；种族间的；按种族划分的
definition_en: connected with a group of people regarded as sharing ancestry; happening between such groups; based on grouping people in that way
core_image: 一张表格上并排列着几个用来勾选族群的方框
scene: 会议室里摊着一份调查报告，讨论的是不同族群在招聘中受到的待遇。 The report called for an end to racial discrimination in hiring.
sceneCN: 这里 racial 是「种族的」（第 1 个义项：与按血统划分的人群有关的）；句意为这份报告呼吁终止招聘中的种族歧视。画面里可留意：摊开的报告、并排的勾选框、沉默的与会者。

pos.zh: 种族的；种族间的；按种族划分的

derivatives.zh: racial 的词根名词，指按血统划分的人群类别
race 加 -ism，指种族歧视与种族主义
race 加 -ist，指带种族歧视态度的
racial 加 -ly，指从种族角度、按种族地

senses.title: Connected with a group by ancestry
senses.definition: relating to a group of people who are regarded as sharing ancestry and physical features
senses.definitionCN: 与被视为共享血统与外貌特征的一群人有关的
senses.example: The law forbids racial discrimination in hiring.
senses.exampleCN: 法律禁止招聘中的种族歧视。
senses.why: The adjective simply adds a relating suffix to the noun race, and the noun itself came from a word for breed.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是在名词 race 后加了表示「相关」的后缀，而那个名词本身来自表示「品种」的词。

senses.title: Happening between such groups
senses.definition: existing or occurring between different groups of people
senses.definitionCN: 存在于不同人群之间或发生在他们之间的
senses.example: Racial tension rose sharply after the election.
senses.exampleCN: 选举之后，族群之间的紧张关系急剧上升。
senses.why: Once the adjective described a group, it could also describe what happens when two such groups meet.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词既能描述一个群体，也就能描述两个这样的群体相遇时发生的事。

senses.title: Based on grouping by ancestry
senses.definition: organized or collected according to categories of ancestry
senses.definitionCN: 按照血统类别来组织或收集的
senses.example: The census collects racial data alongside age and income.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查在收集年龄与收入数据的同时，也收集种族数据。
senses.why: Bureaucracies count people in categories, and a category built on ancestry is described as racial.
senses.whyCN: 行政机构按类别清点人口，而以血统划分的类别就被形容为 racial。

intro.en: Racial is the noun race with the Latin-derived ending -ial; the noun itself came into English through French and Italian from a word of uncertain origin meaning breed.
intro.cn: racial 是名词 race 加上源自拉丁语的词尾 -ial；那个名词本身经法语和意大利语进入英语，来自一个来源不确定、意为「品种」的词。

items.en: Razza meant a breed or a kind, especially of animals, and its own origin is uncertain.
items.cn: razza 意为品种或种类，尤指动物的品种，它本身的来源也不确定。

items.en: French race carried the sense of breed and stock, and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 race 带有「品种、血统」的意思，英语在十六世纪借入。

items.en: English race extended the breed sense to groups of people, a use that later became the subject of scientific debate.
items.cn: 英语的 race 把「品种」义扩展到人群，这一用法后来成为科学争论的对象。

items.en: The ending -ial, from Latin adjective endings, forms words meaning relating to.
items.cn: 词尾 -ial 来自拉丁语形容词词尾，构成意为「与……有关的」词。

items.en: Modern English uses racial for what concerns such groups and for what happens between them.
items.cn: 现代英语用 racial 指与此类群体有关的事，以及发生在它们之间的事。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the noun; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives about peoples and cultures.
note.cn: 形近组收由该名词构成的形式；近义组收表示人群与文化的形容词。

entries.definition: A group regarded as sharing ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为共享血统的一群人。

entries.definition: Prejudice or unfair treatment based on a group.
entries.definitionCN: 基于所属群体的偏见或不公对待。

entries.definition: Showing prejudice against another group.
entries.definitionCN: 对另一群体表现出偏见的。

entries.definition: A person who competes for speed, from the other race.
entries.definitionCN: 参加竞速的人，来自另一个同形的 race。

entries.definition: Relating to a group with shared culture and origin.
entries.definitionCN: 与共享文化和来源的群体有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to a whole country or people.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个国家或民族有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to shared customs and arts.
entries.definitionCN: 与共同习俗和艺术有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to a tribe or tribes.

normalIntro.en: The word is simply race turned into an adjective, so it describes anything done or counted by categories of ancestry.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 race 变来的形容词，因此描述任何按血统类别来做或来清点的事情。

normal.en: Racial is race plus -ial, and -ial is the ending that makes a noun into an adjective of relation.
normal.cn: racial 就是 race 加 -ial，而 -ial 正是把名词变成关系形容词的词尾。

normal.en: Racism is the belief or practice, racial is what relates to groups, and racist describes a person or act.
normal.cn: racism 是信念或做法，racial 指与群体相关的，racist 形容人或行为。

normal.en: Racially is the adverb, as in racially mixed schools.
normal.cn: racially 是副词，如 racially mixed schools（种族混合的学校）。

normal.en: Racial profiling names the practice of suspecting people because of their group.
normal.cn: racial profiling 指因所属群体而怀疑某人的做法。

normal.en: The word has no comparative form because it does not admit degrees.
normal.cn: 这个词没有比较级，因为它不表示程度。

abstract.en: A category becomes an adjective, and the adjective then shapes how people are seen before they are met.
abstract.cn: 一个类别变成了形容词，而这个形容词又在你见到人之前塑造了你如何看待他们。

abstract.en: Words like racial record a way of sorting, and sorting is never only descriptive.
abstract.cn: racial 这样的词记录了一种分类方式，而分类从来不只是描述性的。

abstract.en: Calling something racial can describe a fact and also issue a judgement, depending on the sentence around it.
abstract.cn: 把某事称作 racial，既可能在描述事实，也可能在作出判断，取决于它所在的句子。

examples.en: The school has a clear policy against racial abuse.
examples.cn: 这所学校有明确的规定反对种族侮辱。

examples.en: They collected racial data for the study.
examples.cn: 他们为这项研究收集了种族数据。

examples.en: Racial equality remains a goal rather than a fact in many places.
examples.cn: 在许多地方，种族平等仍是目标而非事实。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐秀」——把人群锐利地分门别类，正好提醒你 racial 是种族的。

root: 意大利语 razza（品种，来源不确定）→ 法语 race（品种、血统）→ 英语 race + -ial → racial；同族有 racism、racist、racially。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a category of ancestry; the senses divide into what belongs to one group, what happens between groups, and what is organized by such categories.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「按血统划分的类别」；义项分为属于某一群体的、发生在群体之间的，以及按这类类别组织的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a form with several boxes for ancestry placed side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张表格上并排放着的几个血统勾选框。

branches.en: a hiring form with a blank for group
branches.cn: 招聘表上一栏留给族群的空格

branches.en: two groups facing each other across a table
branches.cn: 隔着桌子相对的两个群体

branches.en: a census sheet filled in by hand
branches.cn: 手工填写的人口普查表

branches.en: the same category seen from inside and from between
branches.cn: 同一个类别，从内部看与从之间看

branches.en: tension between groups and the counting that records it
branches.cn: 群体间的紧张与记录它的清点

intro.en: The word is a borrowed noun of breed plus a Latin-derived relating suffix, with English endings that build the abstract noun and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是借来的「品种」名词加上源自拉丁语的关系后缀，再加上构成抽象名词与副词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for the noun race itself.
latinIntro.cn: 名词 race 本身没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 细胞核；原子核；核心
definition_en: the central part of a cell or atom, or the core of a group or object
core_image: 一个果核：坚硬的小圆体，所有东西都围着它转
scene: 细胞核里装着它的大部分遗传物质。 The nucleus of a cell contains most of its DNA.
sceneCN: 这里 nucleus 指「细胞核」（第 1 个义项：细胞内保存 DNA 的中央结构）；句意：细胞核保存着细胞的大部分 DNA；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 细胞核；原子核；核心；中心部分；神经核；（音节的）核

forms.label: 果核义（拉丁本义，现代英语少用）

derivatives.zh: 核的；原子核的；细胞核的

senses.title: Cell nucleus
senses.definition: the membrane-bound organelle that contains most of a cell's DNA
senses.definitionCN: 细胞中含有大部分 DNA 的膜结合细胞器
senses.example: The nucleus of a human cell holds twenty-three pairs of chromosomes.
senses.exampleCN: 人类细胞的细胞核里有二十三对染色体。
senses.why: The biological sense was named after the kernel of a nut: a small central body around which the rest is arranged.
