senses.whyCN: 生物学义按坚果的果核命名：一个居中的小体，其余部分围绕它安排。

senses.title: Atomic nucleus
senses.definition: the dense central core of an atom, made of protons and neutrons
senses.definitionCN: 原子中由质子与中子构成的致密中心
senses.example: The nucleus of carbon-12 contains six protons and six neutrons.
senses.exampleCN: 碳-12 的原子核含有六个质子和六个中子。
senses.why: Physics reused the kernel image for the tiny centre of an atom, because almost all its mass sits there.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把果核意象用于原子的微小中心，因为原子几乎全部质量都在那里。

senses.title: Core of a group
senses.definition: the central group of people around whom a larger body forms
senses.definitionCN: 较大群体围绕其形成的核心人群
senses.example: A small nucleus of volunteers kept the project alive.
senses.exampleCN: 一小群志愿者构成的核心让项目维持下去。
senses.why: A group with a hard centre and looser edges matches the kernel image, so the word serves for social structure as well.
senses.whyCN: 一个有坚硬核心与松散边缘的群体符合果核意象，因此这个词也用于社会结构。

senses.title: Central part of an object
senses.definition: the central mass of a comet, crystal or other object
senses.definitionCN: 彗星、晶体或其它物体的中心团块
senses.example: The comet's nucleus is a dirty ball of ice and rock.
senses.exampleCN: 彗核是一个由冰与岩石组成的脏雪球。
senses.why: The word generalises from the kernel to any object's central solid part.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从果核泛化，指任何物体中心那个坚实的部分。

senses.title: Brain nucleus
senses.definition: a cluster of nerve cells in the brain or spinal cord
senses.definitionCN: 脑或脊髓中一簇神经细胞
senses.example: The nucleus accumbens is linked to reward.
senses.exampleCN: 伏隔核与奖赏有关。
senses.why: Anatomists saw clustered cell bodies as kernels inside the nervous tissue, and named them accordingly.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学家把聚在一起的细胞体看作神经组织里的果核，于是如此命名。

senses.title: Syllable nucleus
senses.definition: the vowel or vowel-like sound that forms the centre of a syllable
senses.definitionCN: 构成音节中心的元音或类元音
senses.example: In the word 'cat', the vowel is the syllable nucleus.
senses.exampleCN: 在 cat 这个词里，元音就是音节核。
senses.why: Linguists borrowed the word for the part every syllable must have at its centre, with consonants around it.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家借用这个词，指每个音节中心必须具备的成分，辅音围绕它排列。

senses.title: Galactic nucleus
senses.definition: the dense central region of a galaxy
senses.definitionCN: 星系中央的致密区域
senses.example: The galactic nucleus glows with billions of old stars.
senses.exampleCN: 星系核因数十亿颗老年恒星而发光。
senses.why: Astronomy applies the kernel image at the largest scale, where mass and light concentrate at the centre.
senses.whyCN: 天文学把果核意象用到最大尺度，那里质量与光都集中在中心。

senses.title: Nucleation centre
senses.definition: a small particle or site where a new phase begins to form
senses.definitionCN: 新相开始形成的小颗粒或位点
senses.example: Dust provides the nuclei on which cloud droplets condense.
senses.exampleCN: 尘埃提供了云滴凝结所需的核。
senses.why: A growing crystal or droplet needs a seed at its centre, and the word names that starting point.
senses.whyCN: 生长中的晶体或液滴需要中心的一个种子，这个词就命名那个起点。

senses.title: Nucleus of a collection
senses.definition: the original small set of items around which a larger collection grows
senses.definitionCN: 较大收藏围绕其生长的最初那一小批藏品
senses.example: Six paintings formed the nucleus of the museum's collection.
senses.exampleCN: 六幅画构成了这家博物馆藏品的核心。
senses.why: The kernel image extends to collections: a small hard core of founding items attracts more around it.
senses.whyCN: 果核意象延伸到收藏：一小批创始藏品构成坚硬的核心，吸引更多东西围绕它聚集。

intro.en: Nucleus is Latin for a nut's kernel; science then applied the little central body to cells, atoms, brains and galaxies.
intro.cn: nucleus 在拉丁语里指坚果的果核；科学随后把这个居中的小体用于细胞、原子、脑与星系。

items.en: Latin nux, with the stem nuc-, meant a nut. Its diminutive nucleus meant the small kernel inside a shell.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nux（词干 nuc-）指坚果。其指小形式 nucleus 指壳内的小果仁。

items.en: Nucleus kept the physical sense of a kernel, and by extension any hard central part. English borrowed it in the 17th century.
items.cn: nucleus 保留了果仁的具体意义，并引申指任何坚硬的中心部分。英语在 17 世纪借入。

items.en: Robert Brown described a small body inside plant cells and called it the nucleus in 1831, a term generally credited to him.
items.cn: Robert Brown 在 1831 年描述植物细胞内的一个小体并称之为 nucleus，这一术语一般认为出自他。

items.en: After Rutherford's scattering experiments, the dense centre of the atom was called the nucleus. The date is approximate, around 1911 to 1912.
items.cn: 卢瑟福散射实验之后，原子的致密中心被称为 nucleus。年代约为 1911 至 1912 年。

items.en: The word spread to astronomy, neuroanatomy and linguistics, always keeping the shape of a centre with surrounding parts.
items.cn: 这个词扩散到天文学、神经解剖学与语言学，始终保留「中心加周围部分」的形状。

note.en: The first group separates nucleus from the adjective and from the smaller body inside it; the second separates it from general words for a centre.
note.cn: 第一组把 nucleus 与它的形容词以及它内部更小的结构分开；第二组把它与泛指的「中心」词分开。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of a nucleus'; it is used in nuclear physics and nuclear envelope, while nucleus is the countable noun.
entries.definitionCN: 是形容词，意为「核的」，用于核物理与核膜等；nucleus 是可数名词。

entries.definition: A small structure within the cell nucleus where ribosomes are assembled; it is not the nucleus itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞核内组装核糖体的小结构，不是细胞核本身。

entries.definition: The building block of DNA and RNA; it shares the nuc- root through the idea of a core, but names a molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 指 DNA 与 RNA 的构件；它通过「核心」的观念共享 nuc- 词根，但指的是分子。

entries.definition: The central part of anything, often of an apple or the earth; it is the everyday synonym of nucleus outside science.

entries.definition: The middle point or area of a space; it describes position, not a distinct body with surrounding parts.

entries.definition: The edible part inside a nut, and the literal sense behind nucleus; it is also used figuratively for the essence of a matter.

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: nucleus is Latin for a nut's kernel: the hard thing in the middle.
normal.cn: nucleus 是拉丁语的「果仁」：中间那个硬东西。

normal.en: The family runs nuclear, nucleolus, nucleated, enucleate and nucleation.
normal.cn: 同族词有 nuclear、nucleolus、nucleated、enucleate、nucleation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: cell nucleus, atomic nucleus, comet nucleus, syllable nucleus.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：细胞核、原子核、彗核、音节核。

normal.en: The plural is nuclei, not nucleuses, in scientific writing.
normal.cn: 科学写作中复数用 nuclei，而不用 nucleuses。

normal.en: Every use keeps the same picture: a centre with a surrounding body.
normal.cn: 每个用法都保留同一幅图：一个中心加一个围绕它的整体。

abstract.en: Picture a peach: the stone is the nucleus, the flesh is everything that surrounds it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只桃子：桃核是 nucleus，果肉是围绕它的一切。

abstract.en: An atom is a tiny solar system with the nucleus as its sun.
abstract.cn: 原子像一个微型太阳系，原子核就是它的太阳。

abstract.en: A nucleus of volunteers is a seed crystal around which a project forms.
abstract.cn: 志愿者的核心就是一颗种子晶体，项目围绕它生长。

examples.en: The nucleus stores the cell's chromosomes and controls gene expression.
examples.cn: 细胞核储存细胞的染色体并控制基因表达。

examples.en: Protons and neutrons occupy the atomic nucleus.
examples.cn: 质子与中子占据原子核。

examples.en: A small nucleus of supporters organised the campaign.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nucleus 就是果核」→ 中间那个核 → 细胞核、原子核、核心

root: 拉丁语 nux（坚果，词干 nuc-）→ 指小形式 nucleus「果仁、小核」→ 英语 nucleus；细胞核义始于 1831 年 Robert Brown，原子核义约始于 1911 年。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep one shape: a compact centre surrounded by a larger body. The kernel becomes a cell organelle, an atomic core, a group of people, a comet's heart, a brain cluster, a syllable's vowel, a galactic centre, a seed crystal, and finally the founding core of a collection.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项保持同一种形状：一个紧凑的中心，被更大的整体包围。果仁先后变成细胞器、原子核心、人群核心、彗星中心、脑内细胞簇、音节元音、星系中心、成核种子，最后成为一批藏品围绕其生长的收藏核心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard kernel at the centre, with everything else arranged around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：中央一颗坚硬的果核，其余一切都围着它安排。

branches.en: THE TWO SCIENTIFIC CENTRES: the organelle that holds DNA, and the dense core of the atom.
branches.cn: 两个科学中心：保存 DNA 的细胞器，以及原子的致密核心。

branches.en: SOCIAL AND PHYSICAL CORES: a founding group, and the solid centre of a comet or crystal.
branches.cn: 社会与物理核心：一个创始群体，以及彗星或晶体的坚实中心。

branches.en: ANATOMY AND ASTRONOMY: clustered nerve cells, and the centre of a galaxy.
branches.cn: 解剖与天文：聚成一团的神经细胞，以及星系的中心。

branches.en: LINGUISTICS: the vowel at the centre of a syllable.
branches.cn: 语言学：音节中心的元音。

branches.en: SEED AND SOURCE: the site where growth starts, and the founding core of a collection.
branches.cn: 种子与本源：生长开始的位点，以及一批藏品围绕其生长的收藏核心。

intro.en: Nucleus is a Latin diminutive with no prefix; its family is built with -ar, -olus and -ation.
intro.cn: nucleus 是拉丁语指小词，不带前缀；其词族由 -ar、-olus、-ation 等构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin nux and its diminutive nucleus supply the root. The adjective nuclear adds -ar; nucleolus is a further diminutive; nucleation adds -ation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nux 及其指小形式 nucleus 提供词根。形容词 nuclear 加 -ar；nucleolus 是再一层指小；nucleation 加 -ation。

scene: 孩子跑过来抱住大人的腿，大人弯下腰，用手掌在他背上轻轻拍了两下。 The nurse patted the child's shoulder and told him to breathe slowly.
sceneCN: 这里是「轻拍」（第 1 个义项：用手掌轻轻触碰，多表示安慰）；句意是护士轻拍孩子的肩膀，让他慢慢呼吸。画面里有弯腰的大人和被抱住的孩子。

collocations.zh: 拍拍某人的背以示鼓励

derivatives.zh: 由 pat 与 down 复合而成，指用手掌拍打式的搜身检查
由动词 pat 加 -ing 构成，作名词时指轻拍这一动作

senses.title: To touch lightly with a flat hand
senses.definition: to touch a person or animal gently with the flat of your hand, often to show affection or comfort
senses.definitionCN: 用手掌轻轻触碰人或动物，常用来表达亲切或安慰
senses.example: She patted the dog's head and it wagged its tail.
senses.exampleCN: 她拍了拍狗的头，狗摇起了尾巴。
senses.why: The word probably copies the sound of a light blow, so the first sense is the friendly, sound-sized touch itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很可能在模仿轻拍的声音，所以最早的意思就是这种亲切的、只有一声轻响的触碰。

senses.title: To press or shape something with light blows
senses.definition: to press something flat or into a shape using quick, light movements of the hand
senses.definitionCN: 用手快速而轻的动作把某物压平或压成某个形状
senses.example: Pat the dough into a round ball before you leave it to rise.
senses.exampleCN: 把面团拍成一个圆球，再放着让它发酵。
senses.why: From a friendly touch the same light blow turns into a working motion: the hand does not strike hard, it taps a shape into place.
senses.whyCN: 从亲切的触碰出发，同样轻的一下变成了干活的动作：手并不用力打，只是一下下把形状拍出来。

senses.title: A light blow or its sound
senses.definition: a quick light touch with the hand, or the soft sound it makes
senses.definitionCN: 手掌快速而轻的一下触碰，或它发出的轻微声响
senses.example: He gave the seat a pat to show that I should sit down.
senses.exampleCN: 他拍了拍座位，示意我坐下。
senses.why: The verb becomes a noun by naming one instance of the action, and because the blow is soft, the sound belongs to the sense as well.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成名词，只需指这一个动作的一次；因为这一下很轻，声音也就一并算进了词义。

senses.title: A small flat piece of butter
senses.definition: a small, roughly flat piece of butter or a similar soft food
senses.definitionCN: 黄油或类似软质食物的一小块，大致呈扁平状
senses.example: Melt a pat of butter in the pan before adding the eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 先在锅里化开一小块黄油，再倒入鸡蛋。
senses.why: Butter used to be shaped by hand into small flat pieces, so the word for a light blow came to name the piece you could pat out.
senses.whyCN: 过去黄油常被手工拍成小小的扁块，于是这个表示「轻拍」的词也用来指拍出来的那一小块。

intro.en: Pat has no secure ancient root: the verb is generally thought to imitate the sound of a light blow, and English records it from the Middle Ages onward.
intro.cn: pat 没有可靠的古老词根：一般认为这个动词模仿轻拍的声音，英语自中古时期起就有记录。

items.en: No secure older source is recorded; the verb is generally thought to be imitative of the sound of a light blow.
items.cn: 没有更早的可靠来源记录；一般认为这个动词模仿轻拍所发出的声音。

items.en: Forms such as patten appear in Middle English with the sense of striking or touching lightly.
items.cn: 中古英语中已出现 patten 一类形式，意为轻轻击打或触碰。

items.en: The noun pat names both the light blow and the small sound that comes with it.
items.cn: 近代英语早期，名词 pat 既指这一下轻拍，也指随之而来的轻微声响。

items.en: The phrase a pat of butter is recorded for a small flat piece shaped by patting.
items.cn: 十八世纪出现 a pat of butter 的说法，指拍成的一小块扁平黄油。

items.en: Modern English keeps the word informal and friendly, used for encouragement as well as for shaping things by hand.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个词仍带口语与亲切色彩，既用于鼓励，也用于用手把东西拍出形状。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that echo the same sound or spelling; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for touching and stroking.
note.cn: 形近组收的是声音或拼写相近的短词；近义组收的是表示触碰与抚摸的动词。

entries.definition: A soft cushion or a thick piece of material; only the spelling is close, the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 软垫或厚材料块；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To make a rapid series of light tapping sounds.
entries.definitionCN: 发出连续快速的轻拍声。

entries.definition: A small flat cake of minced food; only the spelling is close, the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 碎肉等做成的小扁饼；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To hit something lightly and quickly, often with a finger.
entries.definitionCN: 常用手指轻而快地敲一下。

entries.definition: To move a hand slowly and gently over something.
entries.definitionCN: 用手缓慢轻柔地抚过某物。

entries.definition: To put a hand or an object lightly against something.
entries.definitionCN: 把手或物体轻轻放在某物上。

normalIntro.en: The word lives on sound and touch at once: a soft smack of the palm that is also a small act of kindness.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时活在声音与触感里：手掌轻轻的一下，也是一点小小的善意。

normal.en: Say pat and you almost hear the sound; the word is built on that soft smack.
normal.cn: 念出 pat，几乎就能听见那一声轻响；这个词就建立在这一下轻拍的声音上。

normal.en: A pat on the back is praise, because the same hand that comforts also congratulates.
normal.cn: a pat on the back 表示称赞，因为安慰人的那只手也用来道贺。

normal.en: Pat dry means to remove water with light touches rather than rubbing.
normal.cn: pat dry 意为用轻按的方式去掉水分，而不是用力摩擦。

normal.en: A pat of butter is the shape produced by patting a soft lump flat.
normal.cn: a pat of butter 就是把软块拍平后得到的形状。

normal.en: The verb doubles its final consonant: patted and patting, so the short vowel stays short.
normal.cn: 这个动词要双写末尾辅音：patted 与 patting，好让短元音保持短促。

abstract.en: A pat lasts less than a second but can carry more comfort than a long speech.
abstract.cn: 轻拍不到一秒，却能比一段长话带来更多安慰。

abstract.en: The word shows how language turns a sound into a gesture and a gesture into a piece of butter.
abstract.cn: 这个词显示了语言如何把声音变成动作，又把动作变成一块黄油。

abstract.en: Anything you can pat is small enough to be handled with care.
abstract.cn: 凡是能用手轻拍的东西，都小到值得被小心对待。

examples.en: She patted the child's back until he stopped crying.
examples.cn: 她轻拍孩子的背，直到他不再哭。

examples.en: Pat the dough flat with the palm of your hand.
examples.cn: 用手掌把面团拍平。

examples.en: He answered with a pat of butter and a slice of bread.
examples.cn: 他回答时递上一小块黄油和一片面包。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拍它」——轻轻拍它一下；pat 就是轻拍。

root: 来源不确定；一般认为模仿轻拍声的拟声词，中古英语已有 patten 一类形式，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a light flat-handed touch; the senses run from comforting a person, to shaping an object, to the blow itself and the small piece it produces.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是手掌平放的一下轻触；义项从安慰他人，到把东西拍出形状，再到这一下本身以及拍出来的小块。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm coming down and lifting again, leaving a soft sound and a little warmth.
core.cn: 核心意象：手掌落下去又抬起，留下一声轻响和一点温度。

branches.en: a hand resting for a second on a child's back
branches.cn: 一只手在孩子背上停留片刻

branches.en: a palm pressing dough into a round shape
branches.cn: 手掌把面团按成圆形

branches.en: the small sound of a hand on a wooden seat
branches.cn: 手掌落在木椅上的轻微声响

branches.en: a curl of butter dropped into a hot pan
branches.cn: 一小块黄油落进热锅

branches.en: comfort and its quiet sound arriving together
branches.cn: 安慰与它轻轻的声音同时到达

intro.en: The word has no ancient root to unpack, so its parts are the English endings it picks up and the phrases it forms.
intro.cn: 这个词没有可拆解的古老词根，因此它的构词成分是它接上的英语词尾和组成的短语。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; the imitative origin has no Latin family behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它的拟声来源背后并没有一个拉丁词族。

definition_zh: 薄雾；水雾；朦胧；蒙上雾气
definition_en: a thin cloud of tiny water droplets near the ground, a fine spray in the air, a blur before the eyes, and the act of covering a surface with such droplets
core_image: 清晨的湖面浮着一层灰白色的薄纱，对岸的树看不清轮廓
scene: 湖面还没有亮起来，对岸的树只剩一层灰影。 A thin mist hid the far shore until the sun rose.
sceneCN: 这里是「薄雾」（第 1 个义项：贴地的稀薄雾层）；句意为一层薄雾遮住远岸，直到太阳升起才散。图中可辨识物件：湖面、灰白的雾层、对岸的树影。

derivatives.zh: 由 mist 加 -y 构成，指有雾的、朦胧的
由 misty 加 -ly 构成，指朦胧地、雾蒙蒙地
由 misty 加 -ness 构成，指有雾、朦胧的状态

senses.title: Thin fog hanging close to the ground
senses.definition: a thin cloud of tiny water droplets near the ground that limits how far you can see
senses.definitionCN: 贴近地面、由细小水珠组成的稀薄雾层，会限制能见距离
senses.example: A cold mist covered the field before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 日出前，一层冷雾盖住了田野。
senses.why: Old English mist named the dimness itself, the grey that hides a distance; the droplets are the modern explanation of what produces that grey, not the starting point of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mist 先指的是「昏暗」本身，是那种把远处藏起来的灰；小水珠只是后人对这片灰的解释，并不是这个词的起点。

senses.title: A fine spray of liquid in the air
senses.definition: a cloud of very small droplets produced by spraying, splashing or cooling
senses.definitionCN: 由喷射、溅洒或冷却产生的细小水滴云
senses.example: A cool mist from the fountain settled on our faces.
senses.exampleCN: 喷泉送来的凉雾落在我们脸上。
senses.why: The same droplets can come from a nozzle or a wave instead of from cooling air; once the eye sees that cloud, the word follows it whatever produced it.
senses.whyCN: 同样的小水珠，可以来自喷头或浪花，而不一定来自空气冷却；眼睛只认那团悬浮的雾，于是词就跟着雾走，不管它是谁造的。

senses.title: A blur in front of the eyes or mind
senses.definition: a blur that keeps something from being seen clearly, especially one made by tears or strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 使某物看不清的一层模糊，尤指眼泪或强烈情绪造成的那种
senses.example: Tears rose and left her eyes in a mist.
senses.exampleCN: 泪水涌起，把她的眼睛蒙成一片朦胧。
senses.why: If mist can hide a field, it can hide anything the eye is trying to see; tears do to the eyes what weather does to a valley, so the word moves indoors.
senses.whyCN: 雾能把一片田野藏起来，就能把眼睛想看的一切藏起来；眼泪对眼睛做的事，正像天气对山谷做的事，于是这个词从户外挪进了眼眶。

senses.title: To cover or become covered with mist
senses.definition: to make a surface, especially glass, collect tiny droplets until it is hard to see through
senses.definitionCN: 使某表面（尤指玻璃）凝上细小水珠，以致看不透
senses.example: The bathroom mirror misted over after the hot shower.
senses.exampleCN: 热水澡之后，浴室的镜子蒙上了一层雾。
senses.why: When a surface collects the same droplets, the noun turns into a verb: the glass does not hold mist, it becomes misty, and English lets the noun carry that change.
senses.whyCN: 当表面凝上同样的小水珠，名词就顺手做了动词：玻璃不是「有雾」，而是「被雾蒙住」，英语让名词直接承担这个变化。

intro.en: Mist is an Old English word for dim air; its deeper origin is uncertain, and it has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: mist 是古英语中表示「昏暗的空气」的词；更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: The reconstructed form *mihstaz meant mist or dimness and is the common Germanic source of the word.
items.cn: *mihstaz 是重构形式，意为雾、昏暗，是这个词在日耳曼语中的共同来源。

items.en: Old English mist named dimness and hazy air, often carrying a sense of darkness as much as of weather.
items.cn: 古英语 mist 指昏暗与朦胧的空气，常常既指天气，也带着「暗」的意味。

items.en: Middle English mist kept the weather sense and began to appear in descriptions of landscape and sea.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mist 保留天气义，并开始出现在风景与海面的描写里。

items.en: Later writers extended the word to any fine cloud of droplets, including spray from water and smoke-like vapour.
items.cn: 后来的作者把词义扩展到任何细小的水珠云，包括水花溅起的雾和烟似的汽。

items.en: Modern English uses mist for thin ground fog, for fine spray, for a blur in the eye, and as a verb for a surface that fogs over.
items.cn: 现代英语用 mist 指贴地的薄雾、细小的水雾、眼前的朦胧，也作动词指表面蒙上雾气。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective and noun built on this stem plus one word that merely looks similar; the near-meaning group gathers other forms of suspended water and the words for heavier or lighter weather.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的形容词与名词，外加一个只是形似的词；近义组收其他悬浮水的形态，以及表示更浓或更轻天气的词。

entries.definition: Full of mist, or seen as if through mist.
entries.definitionCN: 充满雾的；或像隔着一层雾看见的。

entries.definition: In a way that is blurred or covered with mist.
entries.definitionCN: 以朦胧或被雾遮住的方式。

entries.definition: The state of being misty or unclear.
A light, fine drizzle; the spelling is close, but this word has its own origin.
entries.definitionCN: 细小的毛毛雨；拼写相近，但这个词另有来源。

entries.definition: Thicker cloud close to the ground that cuts visibility more sharply.
entries.definitionCN: 贴近地面、更浓的云雾，能见度下降得更厉害。

entries.definition: A light mist, often caused by heat or dust rather than by water alone.
entries.definitionCN: 轻薄的雾，常由热气或尘埃造成，不只是水汽。

entries.definition: Very light rain made of tiny drops.
entries.definitionCN: 由细小水滴构成的毛毛雨。

entries.definition: Hot vapour rising from boiling water that soon turns into droplets.
entries.definitionCN: 沸水升起的热汽，很快又凝成小水珠。

normalIntro.en: Old English used mist for dimness itself, and the family keeps describing what the eye cannot get through.
normalIntro.cn: 古英语用 mist 指「昏暗」本身，这个词族一直在描述眼睛穿不过去的东西。

normal.en: Old English mist named the dimness before it named droplets, so the word began with what the eye loses.
normal.cn: 古英语 mist 先指「昏暗」，后指水珠，所以这个词从「眼睛失去什么」开始。

normal.en: Misty adds -y and turns the noun into the felt quality of a morning.
normal.cn: misty 加 -y，把名词变成早晨能感觉到的那种质地。

normal.en: Mistiness stacks -ness on misty, making the quality itself into something you can name.
normal.cn: mistiness 在 misty 上再叠 -ness，把这种质地本身变成可以命名的东西。

normal.en: The verb mist over keeps the same droplets but moves them onto a surface, which is why a mirror and a valley use the same word.
normal.cn: 动词 mist over 保留同样的水珠，只把它们挪到表面上，所以镜子和山谷用同一个词。

normal.en: Fog, haze and mist differ in thickness and height, not in what they are made of.
normal.cn: fog、haze 与 mist 的差别在浓度和高度，而不在成分。

abstract.en: A word for dimness becomes a word for droplets, and the old feeling survives the new explanation.
abstract.cn: 一个表示昏暗的词变成表示水珠的词，旧的感觉在新解释里活了下来。

abstract.en: Mist on a field and mist in an eye both mean one thing: the distance has stopped being readable.
abstract.cn: 田野上的雾和眼睛里的雾意思相同：距离不再可读。

abstract.en: The smallest drops, too light to fall as rain, are enough to rename a whole morning.
abstract.cn: 小到还落不成雨的水珠，就足以给整个早晨换个名字。

examples.en: A thin mist lay over the lake at dawn.
examples.cn: 黎明时，湖面上浮着一层薄雾。

examples.en: The mirror misted over as the water ran hot.
examples.cn: 热水流下时，镜子蒙上了一层雾。

examples.en: She could not read the road through the mist.
examples.cn: 隔着那层雾，她看不清路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「觅丝」——雾像一层薄薄的丝，缠在眼前，让人「觅」不见路。

root: 古英语 mist（昏暗、雾），更早为重构的日耳曼语形式 *mihstaz；更远的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The senses start from dim air near the ground and spread to any fine droplets, to a blur in the eye, and to the verb for a surface that fogs over.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从贴地的昏暗空气开始，扩散到任何细小的水珠，再到眼前的朦胧，最后到表示表面蒙雾的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey white veil floating on the lake, the far trees reduced to outlines.
core.cn: 核心意象：清晨的湖面浮着一层灰白色的薄纱，对岸的树只剩轮廓。

branches.en: a field erased before sunrise
branches.cn: 日出前被抹掉的田野

branches.en: a fountain throwing cool dust into the air
branches.cn: 喷泉把凉雾甩到空中

branches.en: eyes swimming before a word can be read
branches.cn: 话还没读完，眼睛先模糊

branches.en: a bathroom mirror losing its reflection
branches.cn: 浴室镜子丢掉自己的倒影

branches.en: weather and tears doing the same work to the eye
branches.cn: 天气和眼泪对眼睛做同一件事

intro.en: The word is a Germanic noun for dim air, with English endings that turn it into an adjective, an adverb, a state and a verb.
intro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语中表示昏暗空气的名词，再加英语词尾，可以变成形容词、副词、状态名词和动词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for mist; Latin words for fog, such as nebula, are different words with no shared origin.
latinIntro.cn: mist 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；拉丁语中表示雾的词如 nebula 是另一个词，并无共同来源。

definition_zh: 第九十；九十分之一
definition_en: the ordinal number that comes after the eighty-ninth; one of ninety equal parts
core_image: 一把长尺上刻度密密麻麻，第九十格插着一面小旗
scene: 放学后的教室里，一把长尺摊在桌上，密密麻麻的刻度里，第九十格插着一面小旗。 The ninetieth page of the manuscript is still missing.
sceneCN: 这里是「第九十」（第 1 个义项：计数序列里排在第八十九之后的序数）；句意为手稿的第九十页仍然缺失。图中可辨识物件：长尺、小旗、摊开的手稿。

derivatives.zh: nine 加 -ty 构成基数 ninety，再加 -th 成为 ninetieth，义为「第九十」
由 ninetieth 加 -s 构成的复数，指多个九十分之一

senses.title: The ordinal number after the eighty-ninth
senses.definition: the number that comes after the eighty-ninth in a counted series
senses.definitionCN: 在计数序列中排在第八十九之后的数
senses.example: The ninetieth page of the manuscript is still missing.
senses.exampleCN: 手稿的第九十页仍然缺失。
senses.why: Ninetieth is ninety plus the ordinal ending -th, and ninety itself is nine plus -ty; the whole word counts nine tens and then marks the place at the end of that run.
senses.whyCN: ninetieth 是 ninety 加序数词尾 -th，而 ninety 本身是 nine 加 -ty；整个词数的就是九个十，并标出这一串末尾的位置。

senses.title: One of ninety equal parts
senses.definition: each of the ninety equal parts into which a whole can be divided
senses.definitionCN: 把整体分成九十等份时其中的一份
senses.example: One ninetieth of the land was set aside as a reserve.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地的九十分之一被留作保护区。
senses.why: The ordinal ending both ranks an item and divides a whole, so the same form names the share produced by splitting something ninety ways.
senses.whyCN: 序数词尾既能给事物排位，也能把整体分开，于是同一个形式也用来指把东西分成九十份后得到的那一份。

intro.en: Ninetieth belongs to the native Germanic tens, where a unit numeral plus an ending for a group of ten produced ninety, and the ordinal ending then produced ninetieth.
intro.cn: ninetieth 属日耳曼语本土的十位数：个位数词加上表示「一组十」的词尾造出 ninety，再加序数词尾便得到 ninetieth。

items.en: The Germanic numeral for nine is reconstructed from its later descendants; the exact reconstructed shape is inferred rather than recorded.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的「九」是依据后来的后代形式重构出来的；确切的重构形状属于推断，而不是有记录的词。

items.en: Nigon meant nine and stands at the head of the whole family, including ninety and ninetieth.
items.cn: nigon 意为「九」，是包括 ninety 与 ninetieth 在内的整个词族的源头。

items.en: The ending -tig meant a group of ten, so nigontig counted nine tens and became the ancestor of ninety.
items.cn: 词尾 -tig 表示「一组十」，因此 nigontig 数的是九个十，成为 ninety 的祖先。

items.en: Middle English wrote the tens word as nineti, and the ordinal was formed by adding the usual -th ending.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个十位数写作 nineti，序数形式则由加常见的 -th 词尾构成。

items.en: Modern English has ninetieth for a rank and, much less often, for a ninetieth part.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ninetieth 表示名次，较少用来表示九十分之一。

note.en: The look-alike group walks the same nine base up through its unit, teen, tens and ordinal forms; the near-meaning group sets ninetieth against the ordinals around it on the hundred scale.
note.cn: 形近组沿同一个「九」的底座，从个位、十几、十位走到序数形式；近义组把 ninetieth 放到百的尺度上，与前后相邻的序数对照。

entries.definition: The cardinal that ninetieth ranks, nine tens in one word.
entries.definitionCN: ninetieth 所排的基数，一个词里装着九个十。

entries.definition: The ordinal of nine, the smallest member of the same -th family.
entries.definitionCN: 九的序数词，同一 -th 词族里最小的一员。

entries.definition: The ordinal of nineteen, formed with the teen pattern rather than the tens pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 十九的序数词，用十几的模式而不是十位的模式构成。

entries.definition: The unit numeral that every member of this family starts from.
entries.definitionCN: 整个词族共同出发的个位数词。

entries.definition: The ordinal ten steps below ninetieth on the same scale.
entries.definitionCN: 同一尺度上比第九十低十级的序数词。

entries.definition: The ordinal for one hundred, the next round landmark above ninety.
entries.definitionCN: 一百的序数词，是九十之上下一个整数地标。

entries.definition: A number word that marks position, the class of ninetieth.
entries.definitionCN: 标出位置的数词，ninetieth 所属的类别。

normalIntro.en: The word is a tens numeral wearing a rank ending, and its parts record the two steps that made it: nine tens, then a place at the end of the run.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个披着名次词尾的十位数，它内部的零件记录了造出它的两步：先有九个十，再标出这一串末尾的位置。

normal.en: Ninety is nine tens, so ninetieth marks the last place in the ninth block of ten.
normal.cn: 九十就是九个十，所以 ninetieth 标出第九个十里最后的那一位。

normal.en: The -ty ending in ninety means a group of ten, while -teen in nineteen means ten added on; ninetieth follows the first pattern.
normal.cn: ninety 里的 -ty 表示一组十，而 nineteen 里的 -teen 表示再加十；ninetieth 走的是前一种模式。

normal.en: Adding -th to ninety turns a count into a rank, exactly as fourth is built from four.
normal.cn: 在 ninety 后加 -th，就把计数变成名次，和 fourth 由 four 构成完全一样。

normal.en: The same -th form can also cut a whole into ninety equal shares, giving one ninetieth.
normal.cn: 同一个 -th 形式也能把整体切成九十等份，得到 one ninetieth。

normal.en: In dates and lists the ordinal appears alone, so the ninetieth needs no noun after it.
normal.cn: 在日期和清单里序数词单独出现，所以 the ninetieth 后面不必再跟名词。

abstract.en: Ninety is a number people reach by counting tens, so its ordinal always sounds like the close of a long even run.
abstract.cn: 九十是人们一个个数十才到达的数，所以它的序数听起来总像一长串整齐步子走到收尾。

abstract.en: A word that ranks a page can also name a share of land, because English lets one ending do both jobs.
abstract.cn: 一个能给书页排名的词，也能命名一份土地，因为英语让同一个词尾兼做两件事。

abstract.en: The tens words are the most regular part of English counting, and ninetieth shows the pattern almost without a seam.
abstract.cn: 十位词是英语计数里最规整的部分，而 ninetieth 几乎不带缝隙地展示了这个模式。

examples.en: The ninetieth page of the manuscript is still missing.
examples.cn: 手稿的第九十页仍然缺失。

examples.en: One ninetieth of the land was set aside as a reserve.
examples.cn: 这片土地的九十分之一被留作保护区。

examples.en: They held a party for her ninetieth birthday.
examples.cn: 他们为她的九十岁生日办了聚会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奈恩提阿斯」——长尺量到第九十格，小旗正好插在那里；ninetieth 就是第九十。

root: 古英语 nigon（九）加 -tig（一组十）构成 nigontig（九十），再加序数词尾 -th 得到 ninetieth；与拉丁语 novem 同出原始印欧语数词，但不是借词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a rank at the close of nine tens; the same form also names one of ninety equal parts.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是九个十走完时的一个名次；同一个形式也指九十等份里的一份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long ruler packed with marks, with a small flag planted in the ninetieth slot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把刻满记号的长尺，第九十格里插着一面小旗。

branches.en: the ninetieth page missing from a manuscript
branches.cn: 手稿里缺掉的第九十页

branches.en: a runner counting the laps up to ninety
branches.cn: 跑者一圈圈数到第九十

branches.en: a strip of land reserved from ninety equal shares
branches.cn: 从九十等份里留出的一条土地

branches.en: a number that ranks a page and divides a field
branches.cn: 同一个数既给书页排位，也把田地分开

branches.en: a ninetieth birthday candle standing on a cake
branches.cn: 蛋糕上第九十根生日蜡烛

intro.en: The word is built from the Old English nine, the suffix for a group of ten, the resulting tens numeral and the ordinal ending that ranks it.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的「九」、表示一组十的词尾、由此得到的十位数，以及给它排名的序数词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: English nine and Latin novem descend from the same ancient Indo-European numeral, so the Latin forms are cognates listed for comparison rather than as the source.
latinIntro.cn: 英语的 nine 与拉丁语 novem 同出古老的原始印欧语数词，因此下列拉丁形式只是同源对照，不是来源。
